papers.title: Lax-idempotent monads in homotopy theory
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of lax-idempotent monads to the setting of $(\infty,2)$-categories. In particular, we prove an analogue of Kock and Z\"oberlein's characterization of the category of algebras over a lax-idempotent monad. We then apply this theory to many examples that arise naturally in homotopy theory. For example, we show that $(\infty,1)$-toposes are monadic over presentable $(\infty,1)$-categories, with left adjoint given by the symmetric $(\infty,1)$-topos. We also show that $\infty$-operads are comonadic over symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories through the monoidal envelope construction, obtaining along the way a new proof of Barkan-Steinebrunner's result that the envelope functor is a faithful inclusion. We furthermore use this theory to simplify Ramzi's proof that dualizable stable $(\infty,1)$-categories are comonadic over $\aleph_1$-compactly generated stable $(\infty,1)$-categories.

papers.title: Defect TQFTs, the Generalized Cobordism Hypothesis, and Algebraic $K$-Theory
papers.abstract:
By constructing a fully dualizable category $\mathrm{Bord}^{\mathcal{C}}_n$ as the left adjoint of the forgetful functor, we state a generalized cobordism hypothesis. As a corollary, we establish a generalized Pontryagin-Thom isomorphism that gives a geometric interpretation of higher algebraic $K$-theory using cobordism classes of framed manifolds and stratified spaces decorated by categorical string diagrams, which we call lasagnas. For finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, these decorations are branched local systems.
  We also examine low-dimensional representatives, including $K_1$, Steinberg-group presentations of $K_2$, and fillings related to the Steinberg relation, providing a more explicit construction of Ghys' manifold.

papers.title: Deformations of Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms
papers.abstract:
Recent work of Brantner and Taelman shows that derived deformation theory and period maps can recover strong mixed-characteristic lifting results. In this paper, we develop a prismatic version of this method for Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms, constructing compatible deformations over $A/I^n$ for every $n$ under suitable hypotheses.
  We also apply our method to $F$-split Calabi--Yau varieties over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. In particular, we consider an $F$-split smooth proper variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$, with $H^{d-1}(X,O_X)=0$ and trivial canonical bundle. We show that $X$ admits a lift to $W_3(k)$.

papers.title: Descent and Decomposability of Algebras of Exponent 2 in characteristic 2
papers.abstract: We define an invariant of central simple algebras of degree 8 and exponent 2 over fields of characteristic 2. It is built from the discriminant Pfister forms of symplectic involutions, takes values in a quotient of the third part of the graded group associated to the fundamental filtration of the Witt group of quadratic forms, and vanishes on tensor products of three quaternion algebras, thus giving a necessary condition for decomposability. Variants of the consctuction yield necessary and sufficient conditions for a biquaternion algebra to descend from a quadratic extension of the base field, and for a quaternion algebra to descent from a biquadratic extension that is not purely inseparable. Our results extend known results both in characteristic 2 and in characteristic different from 2, see the introduction. Using residue maps for quadratic forms, we show that these invariants do not vanish in general, and we give an explicit central simple algebra of degree 8 and exponent 2 with nonzero invariant, which is therefore indecomposable. As explained in the appendix, the purely inseparable case is quite different; in particular, a quaternion algebra descents if and only if its Brauer class also does.

papers.title: Homotopy in enriched functor categories: Frobenius exact structures and weak Serre functors
papers.abstract: Let $(\V, \otimes, I,[-,-])$ be a closed symmetric monoidal category with finite (co)limits. Assume that $\V$ is weakly idempotent complete and additive. For a given small $\V$-category $\A$, we investigate sufficient conditions on $\A$ under which the ordinary category $[\A, \V]_0$ of $\V$-functors from $\A$ to $\V$, equipped with the exact structure $\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}}$, is a Frobenius exact category,and hence, induces a triangulated stable category. The exact structure $\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}}$ encompasses the degre-wise trivial exact structure on categories of $N$-chain complexes and $m$-periodic chain complexes, with terms in a variety of settings, including left $R$-modules, quasi-coherent sheaves on a scheme, and Banach spaces. We subsequently address the question of describing abstract left and right homotopy relations in $([\A, \V]_0;\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}})$ in terms of families of morphisms defined objectwise, as in the cases of chain-homotopy and relative homotopy relations. To this end, we introduce the notion of left/right-weak Serre $\V$-functors on $\A$, and investigate their relationships with the classical Serre functor relative to a commutative ring $k$.

papers.title: Motivic invariants of birational hyper-K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that birational projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds have equivalent integral cohomological motives as commutative algebra objects in $\mathrm{SH}(\mathbb C)$. Consequently, their algebraic K-theory spectra are equivalent as $E_\infty$-algebras, and their integral graded K-theory rings are isomorphic.

papers.title: Tate and Artin--Tate Motivic Tensor-Triangular Geometry
papers.abstract: We compute the Balmer spectra of geometric Tate and Artin--Tate motives with $\mathbb{F}_p$-coefficients over any field whose characteristic differs from $p$. For Tate motives, we find the bigraded comparison map to be a homeomorphism to the homogeneous spectrum of the motivic cohomology of the base field. For Artin--Tate motives, we describe the spectrum as a gluing of the spectrum of Artin motives computed by Balmer--Gallauer with the punctured Tate spectrum. We determine all specialisations between these pieces and the resulting topology. Under the hypothesis that the spectrum of rational Tate motives is a singleton, we also compute the integral Tate spectrum after inverting the exponential characteristic of the base field. As a consequence of our results, we identify the punctured Tate spectrum as an open subspace of the spectrum of the category of geometric Voevodsky motives, and draw some conclusions concerning the latter. Finally, we include an appendix where we define generalised periodicity in the context of tensor-triangular geometry, and explore its applications in motivic settings.

papers.title: Gersten injectivity and Morel's purity conjecture
papers.abstract: Morel conjectured that the $\mathbb{A}^1$-homotopy sheaves of an $S^1$-spectrum built from suspension spectra of smooth projective schemes are pure; one condition in purity is injectivity of restriction to dense open subschemes. Over a regular base $S$, we show that this injectivity condition, for the homotopy sheaves of algebraic $K$-theory with coefficients in an arbitrary spectrum, is equivalent to Gersten injectivity at the henselizations of all local rings of smooth $S$-schemes; and that these $K$-theory spectra are pure in Morel's sense. Hence every henselian regular local ring at which Gersten injectivity fails, integrally, rationally, or with finite coefficients, gives a counterexample to Morel's conjecture. The author's finite-coefficient counterexample over $\mathbb{Z}_3[[x,y]]/(3+x^2-y^3)$ therefore disproves the conjecture, already over the regular scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb{Z}[1/2][x,y]/(3+x^2-y^3)$. Recently announced integral and rational Gersten counterexamples, including unpublished work of the author, would show, if confirmed and if they persist after henselization, that the conjecture fails already for the $K$-theory spectrum itself.

papers.title: Initial Subcategories via Free Presentations of the Constant Functor
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category. We characterize the full initial subcategories of $\mathcal{C}$ as precisely those whose representables give a free presentation of the constant functor $\Delta_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbb{K}:\mathcal{C}\to\mathrm{Vect}$. Such a presentation yields a formula for the limit of any functor $\mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}$ as the kernel of a morphism between products of evaluations.
  When the linearized endomorphism ring of every object is local, we show that a minimal free presentation, whenever one exists, determines the unique minimal full initial subcategory, up to equivalence. Bass's characterization of perfect rings gives a sufficient condition for the existence of such presentations. In particular, every finite category with no nonidentity endomorphisms, such as a finite poset, contains a unique minimal initial full subcategory. In the poset case, our results recover the minimal initial subposet constructed in [BDL27] and [DL26]. When $\mathcal{C}$ is the free category on a finite quiver, we give an explicit construction of its minimal initial full subcategories, show that every such subcategory arises from this construction, and provide algorithms with time-complexity bounds.

papers.title: The coanalyticity of the reduced K-theory on modules over free tensor algebras of dualizable t-categories
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formulate Land-Tamme's $\boxtimes$-construction and $\odot$-construction for continuous exact monads on dualizable stable $\infty$-categories, and establish the behaviour of localizing invariants on pushouts of left modules over continuous exact monads on dualizable stable $\infty$-categories. Combining the Land-Tamme theory of continuous exact monads with the theory of analytic functors in Goodwillie calculus, we show that the reduced K-theory on modules over free tensor algebras of dualizable t-categories is modified 1-coanalytic or modified 2-coanalytic, depending on the coconnectivity of the base algebras. In particular, this answers Efimov's question concerning coanalyticity in the affirmative.

papers.title: An odd version of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra and the odd Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
papers.abstract: We study an ``odd'' version of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra that is obtained by replacing free Lie algebras in even generators by free graded Lie algebras in odd generators in the classical definition. These odd variants are related to the ``odd'' Kontsevich graph complex in the same way as the classical Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group is related to the even Kontsevich graph complex. We show an odd analog of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, namely that the odd Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra is isomorphic to a free graded Lie algebra in one odd generator of weight 3. Thus we in particular compute the odd graph cohomology in the bottom cohomological degree, showing that it is mostly zero.

papers.title: Higher limits over the fusion orbit category via subgroup complexes
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a saturated fusion system over a finite $p$-group $S$, and $\mathcal{O}^c (\mathcal{F})$ denote the centric orbit category of $\mathcal{F}$. Suppose that $G$ is a discrete group realizing $\mathcal{F}$, and $\mathcal{C}$ is the collection of all $p$-centric subgroups in $G$. We prove that for every $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)} \mathcal{O} ^c (\mathcal{F})$-module $M$, the higher limits $\lim ^* _{\mathcal{O}^c (\mathcal{F})} M$ are isomorphic to the equivariant cohomology $H_ G ^* (|\mathcal{C}| ; \mathcal{M} )$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is the $G$-equivariant coefficient system on $|\mathcal{C}|$ induced by $M$. This is the fusion system version of a theorem by Grodal for higher limits over the $p$-orbit category $\mathcal{O}_p(G)$ of a finite group $G$. As a consequence, for every fusion system $\mathcal{F}$, we obtain a finite sequence of cohomology groups, involving the cohomology of $\mathcal{F}$, which is exact if and only if the mod-$p$ subgroup decomposition for $\mathcal{F}$ over $\mathcal{F}$-centric subgroups is sharp.

papers.title: Landscape Intervals: A Geometric Framework for Multiparameter Persistence Landscapes
papers.abstract: Classical persistent homology provides a summary of the multiscale topology of a filtration of a space. These summaries are not naturally valued in a vector space, limiting their direct use in standard machine learning pipelines. To address this issue, Bubenik introduced persistence landscapes, vector-valued invariants of persistence modules, which operate by conveniently encoding the behavior of rank functions of modules along the parameter axis. When passing to multiparameter persistent homology, changes in the rank functions vary by different amounts in different directions. In this paper, we introduce the landscape interval, a subset of the parameter space of a multiparameter persistence module which records changes in the rank function in all directions simultaneously. This geometric perspective leads to two novel invariants which serve as notions of persistence landscapes for multiparameter modules. We show that our invariants generalize existing landscape-type invariants: in particular, they recover Bubenik's landscapes in the one-parameter setting and allow us to obtain the multiparameter landscapes introduced by Vipond. For our main theoretical contributions, we establish two exact identities connecting landscapes with erosion distances, prove that our invariants are stable under perturbations, and refine the interleaving-stability bounds for the existing landscape-type invariants. We also show that on a certain class of multiparameter persistence modules, the full invariants can be recovered from finite information about the module. On the practical side, we introduce a robust numerical framework for extracting our invariants from real data and for incorporating them into standard machine learning pipelines. The framework is illustrated on surface mesh and medical image data.

papers.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
papers.abstract:
Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$.
  The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $\iota_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincar\'e duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.

papers.title: $K$-tropical curves, Riemann-Roch and Serre duality
papers.abstract: We endow a tropical curve with the structure of a ringed space and establish analogues of Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for these ringed spaces. As a corollary, we give a cohomological proof of the tropical Riemann-Roch theorem.

papers.title: A 7/8 zero-free half-plane for angular Hecke L-functions over the Eisenstein field
papers.abstract: We reconstruct the argument recorded in a frozen Lean development establishing nonvanishing of the unit-compatible angular Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$ in the strict half-plane $\Re(s)>7/8$, apart from the genuine principal pole. The family includes every admissible integer angular order, all nonzero finite ideal moduli, primitive and imprimitive presentations, and real unitary norm twists. This strengthens the earlier $15/16$ result for the same angular family. The proof compares two estimates for a single normalized physical probe: a low bound with exponent $3/16+\omega$ and an approximation by a reciprocal Mellin signal with error exponent $\beta_n-11/16-\sigma$, where $\beta_n$ is the supremum of the real parts of zeros within a finite angular cap. Crucially, the positive saving $\sigma$ is chosen before the target character. Mellin continuation converts these estimates into a strict improvement of the zero supremum. Induction on angular order, together with conjugation, establishes nonvanishing for the full family. The repaired public proof closure passed a clean compilation of 8,213 Lean modules and fresh native Lean kernel replay. An independent AI-assisted audit recorded five ACCEPT verdicts for the repaired package, following the identification and correction of a reproducibility defect in the original archive. We document the mathematical argument, formal verification evidence, and remaining limitations. This manuscript is an expository reconstruction, not independent human mathematical certification. We describe the formally verified proof as a *xenoproof* and the result provisionally as a *xenotheorem*, distinguishing machine-checkable correctness from established human mathematical understanding.

papers.title: A certified upper bound for the distortion of the trefoil knot
papers.abstract: The distortion of a rectifiable closed curve $\gamma\subset\mathbb R^3$ is the supremum, over pairs of distinct points, of the ratio of the length of the shorter arc of $\gamma$ between them to their distance; the distortion $\delta(K)$ of a knot type $K$ is the infimum over all curves of type $K$. For the trefoil, the published lower bound is $\delta\ge5\pi/3$, valid for every non-trivial knot (a recent preprint claims $\delta>6.5321$), and the only upper bound we found in the literature is the value $7.16$ obtained by numerical simulation. We exhibit an explicit polygon with $192$ vertices, of knot type trefoil, whose distortion is at most $6.92$. The proof is computer-assisted: the knot type is certified by an explicit piecewise-linear path of embedded polygons starting from a polygon on a torus, and the distortion by exact rational arithmetic on every pair of edges. Two separately written verifiers are supplied.

papers.title: A closed-form bound for linear forms in three $p$-adic logarithms of rational numbers
papers.abstract: We deduce from the $p$-adic kit for three logarithms of the companion note hexagon:2610.00706 a fully explicit bound in closed form. If $\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3$ are multiplicatively independent rationals, congruent to $1$ modulo $p$ (modulo $4$ if $p=2$), of heights at most $a_j\log p$ with $a_j\ge1$, and if $|b_j|\le B$, then $v_p(\gamma_1^{b_1}\gamma_2^{b_2}\gamma_3^{b_3}-1)\le a_1a_2a_3\,\mathcal{B}^2\max\{27\,711,\ C_2(p)\max_j a_j\}$, where $\mathcal{B}=\max\{\log B/\log p,\,10\}$ and $C_2(p)=11\,107\,\frac{p}{p-1}\bigl(1+\frac{0.31}{\log p}\bigr)^2$, as soon as $\gamma_1^{b_1}\gamma_2^{b_2}\gamma_3^{b_3}\ne1$. By a change of basis in the multiplicative group, the result applies to arbitrary rationals prime to $p$. On the examples of that note, the bound is $42$ to $956$ times smaller than that of Yu's explicit theorem, and stays within a factor between $1.2$ and $2.5$ of the numerical optimisation of the parameters of the kit.

papers.title: A general equivalence relation on the global class of morphisms of a category
papers.abstract: We introduce a general equivalence relation on the global class of morphisms of a category that subsumes several classical notions of equivalence in mathematics. We show that group-action equivalence relations, pullback equivalence relations, and coarse analysis-operator-based equivalence relations on continuous Bessel families are special cases of this general definition.

papers.title: A kit for linear forms in three $p$-adic logarithms
papers.abstract: We transpose to the $p$-adic case the kit of Mignotte and Voutier for linear forms in three logarithms. The new tool is a lower bound for the $p$-adic valuation of interpolation determinants with no factorial loss: it is obtained by expanding the powers $\theta^{\ell z}$ as binomial series in $\theta-1$, and then transporting an order of vanishing that we compute optimally for generic points, by means of the initial forms of the space of exponential polynomials involved. It holds for every prime $p$. Combined with a rearrangement bound for the spread of the exponents and with Gouillon's zero lemma applied within a Teichmüller class, it gives a criterion of the form of criterion (2.8) of Mignotte–Voutier, in which $\log\rho$ is replaced by $\log p$ and the height term contains no analytic contribution. For two logarithms, in $\mathbb{Q}_p$ with $p$ odd, it improves Lemma 8 of Bugeaud–Laurent. A change of basis in the multiplicative group reduces to the case of principal units: the factor $g=p-1$ leaves the volumes and moves into the heights. On examples, with exponents up to $10^{10}$ or $10^{30}$, the complete bounds (degenerate cases included) are $154$ to $667$ times smaller than those of Yu's explicit theorem for $p\in\{5,13\}$, $608$ to $1980$ times for $p\in\{7,11\}$ (where the explicit form of Yu goes through $\mathbb{Q}(i)$), and $73$ to $105$ times for $p=101$.

papers.title: A Koteljanskii inequality for permanents
papers.abstract: We prove a permanental analogue of Koteljanskii's inequality. If $A$ is an inverse $M$-matrix that becomes symmetric after a positive diagonal similarity, then $\mathrm{per}(A_{S\cup T})\,\mathrm{per}(A_{S\cap T})\ge\mathrm{per}(A_S)\,\mathrm{per}(A_T)$ for all $S,T\subseteq[n]$, where $A_S$ is the principal submatrix indexed by $S$. The proof expresses permanents as moments of a complex Gaussian vector and uses Ginibre's correlation inequality. Finally, an explicit counterexample shows that symmetry cannot be dropped.

papers.title: A natural Chow lemma for smooth threefolds and fourfolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth proper integral variety of dimension at most four over a field of characteristic zero. We construct a finite sequence of blowups along smooth centers with projective endpoint, preserving the intersection of all maximal quasi-projective opens of $X$. The construction depends only on a fixed functorial principalization procedure and is natural under isomorphisms, including those over different ground fields. The proof has two parts. A colength argument on regular local surfaces gives, in every dimension, a finite preparation after which some maximal quasi-projective open has complement mapping into codimension at least three in $X$. In dimensions at most four these images are points or curves. Ample numerical classes on the normalized components of that complement give finite bounds for summing base ideals of linear systems. The resulting ideal descends to the original field; geometric integrality is not required.

papers.title: A note on rational wavefront sets for finite special orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: We study rational wavefront sets of irreducible representations of finite special orthogonal groups over $\mathbb F_q$. We assume that $q$ is odd and that both $q$ and its characteristic are sufficiently large. Using {the second author's} results for full orthogonal groups, we determine the maximal rational wavefront sets and the dimensions of the corresponding generalized Whittaker models. We show that each rational wavefront set is the rational closure of its maximal elements. For unipotent representations, we describe the maximal rational wavefront sets in terms of Lusztig's canonical quotient and their behavior under Alvis--Curtis duality.

papers.title: A Proof of Petz's Conjecture on the Scalar Curvature of the Kubo–Mori Metric
papers.abstract: Petz (1994) conjectured that the scalar curvature of the Kubo–Mori metric on invertible density matrices increases as the state becomes more mixed. Dittmann (2000) reduced the conjecture to the concavity of an explicit symmetric function $h$ on $(0,\infty)^3$. We prove that $h$ is strictly concave, and hence Petz's conjecture. The proof writes $h=-1/(8M)$ with $M$ positive and homogeneous of degree one, and its central idea is to show that $t\mapsto 1/M(X+tY)$ is a Stieltjes function for all $X,Y>0$; Cauchy–Schwarz and homogeneity then give concavity of $h$ on $(0,\infty)^3$.

papers.title: A sharp Brégman–Minc bound for permanents
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp Brégman–Minc bound for permanents of nonnegative matrices that was conjectured by Samorodnitsky and Gurvits. Specifically, for $\phi(x)=\Gamma(1+1/x)^{-x}$, with $\phi(0)=0$, applied entrywise, we show that every nonnegative row-stochastic square matrix $A$ satisfies $\operatorname{per}\phi[A]\le1$, which is the Brégman–Minc inequality when each row of $A$ is uniform on its support. The crux of our proof is a scalar inequality on the simplex, which we prove using a carefully chosen yet elementary integral representation. We note brief applications to the entropy of a random permutation and to sharp bounds for rectangular permanents and matchings.

papers.title: A stacky resolution of singularities for orders by Azumaya algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a stacky resolution of singularities for certain noncommutative spaces which can be viewed as 'finite noncommutative extensions' of schemes. More precisely, we show that any order over a reduced separated finite type scheme over a field of characteristic zero can be resolved by an Azumaya algebra over a smooth Deligne--Mumford stack by a sequence of stacky blow-ups.

papers.title: A Sublinear Treewidth Exponent for Binary Constraint Satisfaction
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for binary constraint satisfaction whose exponent in the input size is sublinear in treewidth on a class of graphs with unbounded treewidth. There are a class G of graphs of bounded maximum degree, a constant c, and a function f such that one algorithm correctly decides every binary CSP instance and, on instances I with primal graph G ∈ G, runs in time f(G) · ||I||^(c · tw(G) / sqrt(log tw(G))) . This contradicts the literal formulation of Conjecture 1.4 of Marx (2010). The algorithm follows from a domain-uniform counting bound: for every fixed maximum degree ∆, complete-table in- stances with k variables and domain size D ≥ 2 can be counted in time LO∆ (1)DO∆ (k/√log k) for suﬃciently large k. The constants are independent of D and of the constraint relations. We obtain this bound from the tensor-network recursion of Claude (Anthropic), and use attributed graph foundations from OpenAI to construct the required expander family. Support pruning connects the counting routine to sparse tuple-list inputs without expanding the original domain. The algo- rithm, its native finite-alphabet machine implementation, and the conjecture counterexample are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: A Tropical Viewpoint on the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a tropical perspective on the recent arguments announced by OpenAI for Nagata's conjecture and the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg conjecture. By degenerating to both the normal cone and a semistable model whose dual graph is a cycle, we replace sections on a surface by Laurent polynomials in two variables. In place of theta functions, tropical methods bound the exponents of these Laurent polynomials, and a lift of the tropical Abel--Jacobi class of the normal bundle controls the shape of the resulting exponent diagram. Combining these support bounds with interpolation on a torus proves the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg conjecture with its predicted threshold whenever the corresponding linear series contains an integral curve whose only singularity is an ordinary node that is not a basepoint.

papers.title: Abelianization and moment maps
papers.abstract: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $\mu$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$. We do this by looking at the restriction of $\mu$ to an intermediate space $Z/T \subset X_T$, where $Z/G=X_G$. We show that the generic fibres of this map are co-Lagrangians that project to Lagrangians on $X_G$. We completely describe the image in the case where $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$, and show that in the general $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$ case the image can be sliced so that each piece is determined by a finite set of points, related to matroid circuits.

papers.title: Alcove walks, crystal structure and a Levi branching rule
papers.abstract: In the Borel case $P=B$, we endow Haines' set of maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks (arXiv:2405.17174) with a crystal structure. We construct a bijection with the LS-gallery model of Gaussent and Littelmann (arXiv:math/0307122) and prove that it intertwines the root operators. This answers a question raised by Haines. We also extend the Gaussent-Littelmann stratification to the parabolic setting, prove the Levi branching rule for LS galleries, and compare the resulting gallery model with Haines' maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks in the parabolic setting.

papers.title: Algebraic tori in the complement of quartic surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $B\subset \mathbb{P}^3$ be an slc quartic surface. The existence of an embedding $\mathbb{G}_m^3\hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^3\setminus B$ implies that $B$ has coregularity zero. In this article, we initiate the classification of coregularity zero slc quartic surfaces $B\subset \mathbb{P}^3$ for which $\mathbb{P}^3\setminus B$ contains an algebraic torus $\mathbb{G}_m^3$, and equivalently, the classification of cluster type pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3,B)$. Along the way, we give criteria for a log Calabi--Yau pair $(X,B)$ over a toric variety $T$ to be of cluster type.

papers.title: An atomic approach to Shokurov's conic-bundle conjecture
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply a weaker version of Hodge atoms to show that a standard conic bundle over a smooth complex projective rational surface $S$ is irrational if $|2K_S+\Delta|\ne\emptyset$, where $\Delta$ is the discriminant divisor. This proves Shokurov's conjecture on rationality of conic bundle threefolds. As an application, we deduce precisely which nodal quartic double solids are rational.

papers.title: An Improved Subexponential Bound for Deterministic Integer Factorization
papers.abstract: We prove that the complete prime factorization of an $n$-bit integer can be computed deterministically in time $2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ and polynomial space. This establishes the bound conjectured by Rudich and Rousseau, sharpening their qualitative $N^{o(1)}$ result. The proof combines OpenAI's quantitative Boolean tensor-contraction theorem with the linear-size multiplication encoding of Akshima et al. The encoding permits exact counting of divisors with prescribed binary prefixes without loss in the exponent. The least prime factor is then recovered by successive prefix queries, and iteration yields the complete factorization within the same asymptotic bound.

papers.title: An optimal multiplicity estimate for interpolation determinants in three logarithms
papers.abstract: In the kit of Mignotte and Voutier for linear forms in three logarithms, the order of vanishing at the origin of the interpolation determinant is bounded below by Waldschmidt's general multiplicity lemma; the authors indicate that this estimate should be improvable. We give a lower bound for this order which is optimal for generic points. The functions involved span a space whose initial forms are described by a uniqueness property for a linear differential equation with constant coefficients. As a consequence, the left-hand side of their criterion (2.8) can be taken equal to $\frac{(2K+1)(L-1)}{3}\log\rho$, with main term $\frac{2KL}{3}\log\rho$ instead of $\frac{KL}{2}\log\rho$. On the two examples of their paper, with their public code modified in one line and the conditions of the zero lemma checked, the bounds given by the criterion go from $17.94\cdot10^6$ to $4.79\cdot10^6$ and from $28.85\cdot10^6$ to $7.00\cdot10^6$. The same estimate is the multiplicity input of our kit for three $p$-adic logarithms.

papers.title: Asymptotic geometry of non-abelian Hodge theory and Riemann--Hilbert correspondence, rank three $\widetilde{E}_6$ case
papers.abstract: We prove the Geometric P=W conjecture in rank 3 on the three-punctured sphere. We describe the topology at infinity of the related character variety. We use asymptotic abelianization of harmonic bundles away from the ramification divisor and an equivariant approach near the branch points to find the WKB (also known as Liouville--Green or phase-integral) expansion of the involved maps. We analyze the Stokes phenomenon governing their behavior.

papers.title: Baker--Akhiezer sections from Higgs bundles and Landau levels in hyperbolic band theory
papers.abstract: As observed by Kienzle and the second author, rank-two $\mathcal{O}(3)$-twisted Higgs bundles on the projective line encode all hyperbolic crystals of genus two: the spectral curves are the unit cells, and the Hitchin fibers are the abelian Brillouin zones. In a uniform magnetic field of two flux quanta, the lowest Landau level is one-dimensional at every nonzero momentum, and, as found by Iengo and Li, its dimension jumps to two at the zero momentum. We identify the states of the lowest Landau level with the Baker--Akhiezer sections of the Higgs bundles, and their zeros, the vortices, with the Baker--Akhiezer divisors. A family of nonzero momenta limits to the zero momentum exactly when each of the two vortices approaches the image of the other under the spatial inversion, and the states of the jumped level are labeled by the directions of limiting. On the Higgs bundle side, the zero momentum is the point where the Hitchin fiber intersects the Hitchin section. Such a family of Higgs bundles limits to the Hitchin section, thereby crossing to a lower stratum of the \BB stratification, an example of the phenomenon investigated in terms of Baker--Akhiezer divisors by the first author with Figiel and Teschner.

papers.title: Beyond Small Balls: A Determinant Inequality for Functions of Matrix Gaussian Series
papers.abstract: We prove a functional extension of Gaussian operator-norm small-ball inequalities. Let $X=\sum_{i=1}^d g_iB_i$, where $g\sim N(0,I_d)$, the matrices $B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ are symmetric, and $\sum_iB_i^2\preceq I_d$. For every even log-concave $f\colon\mathbb{R}\to[0,\infty)$, we obtain $\mathbb{E}\det f(X)\ge(\mathbb{E} f(\kappa G))^d$ at dilation $\kappa=13/5$, where $G$ is standard Gaussian. The proof reduces each function to one small-ball estimate, obtained from matrix-weighted Poincaré inequalities, and controls the rest by averages over the spectrum. We give an equivalent entropy formulation. An explicit counterexample shows that no universal dilation below $\sqrt{\pi/2}$ can work; we conjecture that this value is optimal.

papers.title: Birational geometry of log Calabi-Yau pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3, D)$ of coregularity 2
papers.abstract: This paper aims to study the birational geometry of log Calabi-Yau pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3, D)$ of coregularity 2, where in this case $D$ is an irreducible normal quartic surface with canonical singularities. We completely classify which toric weighted blowups of a point will initiate a volume preserving Sarkisov link starting with this pair. Depending on the type of singularity, our results point out that some of these weights do not work generically for a general member of the corresponding coarse moduli space of quartics.

papers.title: Bounded Bruhat intervals and affine Coxeter groups
papers.abstract: Dyer (1991) proved that, for each fixed length $k$, only finitely many isomorphism types of Bruhat intervals occur in finite Coxeter groups. In this short paper, we prove that this result holds also for affine Coxeter groups, and moreover that this characterizes the affine groups among all infinite Coxeter groups. We also show that the coefficients of $q$ in the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of a Coxeter group are bounded if and only if the group is finite or affine.

papers.title: Brauer graph algebras are closed under stable equivalence of Morita type
papers.abstract: We study stable equivalences of Brauer graph algebras. We prove that a basic symmetric algebra without semisimple summands which is stably equivalent to a Brauer graph algebra is again a Brauer graph algebra. In particular, Brauer graph algebras are closed up to semisimple summands under stable equivalence of Morita type. As consequences, we reprove the closure under derived equivalence established by Antipov and Zvonareva and obtain a solution of the reconstruction problem posed by Rickard and Rouquier for algebras stably equivalent of Morita type to Brauer graph algebras.

papers.title: Certified ropelength bounds for torus knots and the tight knot constant
papers.abstract: The tight knot constant $\alpha_0$ is the largest constant with $L(K)\ge\alpha_0\,\mathrm{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$ for every knot $K$, where $L$ is the ropelength (unit-radius rope) and $\mathrm{Cr}$ the crossing number. We exhibit an explicit $C^{1,1}$ embedding of the torus knot $T(19,24)$, with $\mathrm{Cr}=432$, of thickness at least $1$ and length at most $939.984$. Hence $\alpha_0\le 9.9200$. The published bound is $10.76$. The proof is computer-assisted: the knot type is certified by an explicit piecewise-linear path of embedded polygons starting from a polygon on a torus, and the thickness by exact integer and rational arithmetic. Two separately written verifiers are supplied, together with certificates for $T(14,17)$ and $T(11,14)$.

papers.title: Changing parameters in Hall-Littlewood functions
papers.abstract: We study the transition coefficients $b_{\lambda,\mu}(q,t)$ of the Hall--Littlewood $P$-functions $P_\lambda(t)$ expanded in the basis $P_\mu(q)$. We find a tableaux formula when $\lambda$ is a hook shape which generalizes term-by-term Lascoux-Schutzenberger's charge formula as well as Macdonald's monomial expansion formula for Hall-Littlewood functions. We conjecture that $b_{\lambda,\mu}(t+1,t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ and prove it when $\lambda$ is a hook shape, when $\lambda$ has two-columns and some more simple cases. We prove that $b_{\lambda,\mu}(t+n,n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$, extending work of Alexandersson, and we record a stability property and some reduction principles.

papers.title: Characteristic polynomials and eigenvalues of tensors
papers.abstract: We lay the geometric foundations for the study of the characteristic polynomial of tensors. For symmetric tensors of order $d \geq 3$ and dimension $2$, and symmetric tensors of order $3$ and dimension $3$, we prove that only finitely many tensors share any given characteristic polynomial, unlike the case of symmetric matrices and the case of non-symmetric tensors. We propose precise conjectures for the dimension of the variety of tensors sharing the same characteristic polynomial, in the symmetric and non-symmetric settings.

papers.title: Claw-free perfect graphs are chromatic-choosable.
papers.abstract: We prove that every claw-free perfect graph $G$ satisfies $\ch(G)=\chi(G)=\omega(G)$. More strongly, if $S$ is a clique of simplicial vertices of $G$ and $k\ge\omega(G)$, every proper precoloring of $S$ extends to a proper coloring of $G$ from arbitrary lists of size $k$ on $V(G)\setminus S$. The proof has three coloring steps: a mixed-list theorem for cobipartite graphs, a precoloring-extension theorem for elementary graphs built on Galvin's kernel method and a homogeneous-pair exchange argument, and a polynomial method (Combinatorial Nullstellensatz) argument for graphs of interval type in which a Vandermonde factor is transferred across each incomplete pair. The three coloring steps are assembled along the structure theorems of Chv\'atal--Sbihi, Maffray--Reed and Chudnovsky--Seymour, using double clique cutsets for composition. As a consequence, every perfect line graph is chromatic-choosable, recovering the theorem of Peterson and Woodall. Our precoloring extension theorem also resolves a conjecture posed by Chudnovsky and Seymour.

papers.title: Closed Colored Models and Demazure Crystals
papers.abstract:
We construct and study solvable lattice models whose partition functions are Demazure characters. Two types of colored generalizations of the five-vertex model can be defined that are called the open and closed models. States of both models are associated with Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns, or equivalently, semistandard Young tableaux. We characterize the tableaux arising from states of the closed model and prove that they form a Demazure crystal. This is stronger than identifying the partition function as a Demazure character: it requires constructing Kashiwara crystal operators on the states through lattice moves and recoloring. For the open model, Brubaker, Bump, Buciumas, and Gustafsson showed that the states realize (crystal) Demazure atoms. We also give a new, independent proof of their result.
  Bump and Naprienko considered bosonic models involving a parameter t. In these models, the edges and vertices are constructed by fusion of simpler edge and vertex types. Taking t=0 produces bosonic analogs of the open model. By reversing the fusion order, we construct closed bosonic models and establish their Yang-Baxter equations, yielding a Demazure-Lusztig recursion for the partition functions. At t=0, these models specialize to bosonic analogues of the closed five-vertex model, and we prove that their states form Demazure crystals.

papers.title: Coincidences of $q$-analogues of Markoff numbers outside the known families: an answer to a question of Labbé, Lapointe and Steiner
papers.abstract: Labbé, Lapointe and Steiner proved that $w\mapsto\mu_q(w)_{12}$ is injective on Christoffel words, gave two families of identities showing that it is not injective on $\{\mathtt{0},\mathtt{1}\}^*$, and asked whether every coincidence $\mu_q(x)_{12}=\mu_q(y)_{12}$ comes from these two families. We show that it does not. The smallest counterexamples have length $24$; by an exhaustive computation, among words of length at most $32$ there are exactly $50$ classes of coincidences not explained by the two families, $10$ of length $24$ and $40$ of length $30$. Each of them contains an instance of one of a few new identities, which we prove for a generic $2\times2$ matrix in place of the matrix of a factor of the word. One of these identities belongs to an infinite family, indexed by $k\equiv1\pmod 4$, which we prove for every such $k$.

papers.title: Composing Double Categories
papers.abstract:
Many kinds of generalised syntax, including internal categories, T-categories or polynomial monads, arise as monads in bicategories of a certain flavour: maps are some kind of span, and composition is some kind of pullback. We explain the pattern behind these similarities: each bicategory is stitched together from two simpler pieces by a distributive law, where the distributivity is governed by pullback.
  A key novelty is in the kind of distributive law we consider; where Rosebrugh and Wood considered distributive laws between categories, we instead consider pseudo-distributive laws between double categories. A key construction, drawing on work of Weber, obtains such a distributive law from a so-called co-crossed double category: one whose codomain functor is a fibration, and whose cartesian cells are stable under horizontal composition.
  We show the horizontal Kleisli double category of a monad T is co-crossed just when T is cartesian, and that the composite double category recovers T-spans; that the double category associated to an identity-on-objects functor is co-crossed just when that functor is a calibration in the sense of B\'enabou; and that Street's calibrated bicategories yield co-crossed double categories in a similar manner, recovering the double category of polynomials of Gambino--Kock.

papers.title: Composition factor algebras and finite representation type
papers.abstract: An Artin algebra is called a composition factor algebra if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. We prove that every composition factor algebra is representation-finite. This settles a conjecture of Auslander, Reiten and Smal\o. We also give criteria for comma categories and factorization categories to be of finite representation type.

papers.title: Constructing and transforming standard resolutions of local modules
papers.abstract: We construct standard resolutions for analytic local modules on complex hypersurfaces using standard basis methods, with extensions to complete intersections. The algebraic version over arbitrary infinite fields is also suggested. Applications include derived category formula of local hypersurface blow-ups, revealing new connections between standard bases and categorical geometry.

papers.title: Curved $\infty$-Local Systems And Projectively Flat Riemann-Hilbert Correspondence
papers.abstract: We generalize the higher Riemann-Hilbert correspondence in the presence of scalar curvature for a (possibly non-compact) smooth manifold $M$. We show that the dg-category of curved $\infty$-local systems, the dg-category of graded vector bundles with projectively flat $\mathbb Z$-graded connections and the dg-category of curved representations of the singular simplicial set of the based loop space of $M$ are all $A_\infty$-quasi equivalent. They provide dg-enhancements of the subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant and have finite-dimensional fibers. In the ungraded case, we reduce to an equivalence between projectively flat vector bundles and a subcategory of projective representations of $\pi_1(M; x_0)$. As an application of our general framework, we also prove that the category of cohesive modules over the curved Dolbeault algebra of a complex manifold $X$ is equivalent to a subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules which generalizes a theorem due to Block to possibly non-compact complex manifolds.

papers.title: Decomposing super unitary representations using Berezin integration
papers.abstract: I introduce the notion of a family of super unitary representations depending upon odd parameters as well as the notion of a direct Berezin integral of such representations. I use this to decompose the (left-)regular representation of the super Heisenberg group and of a super Heisenberg-like group into smaller (irreducible) subrepresentations. I compare the obtained subrepresentations to the representations obtained by applying (super) geometric quantization of the coadjoint orbits of the corresponding groups. It turns out that for the super Heisenberg group we need coadjoint orbits with an odd symplectic form in order to describe all subrepresentations found in the decomposition and for the Heisenberg-like super group we even need orbits with a non-homogeneous symplectic form.

papers.title: Degeneration of Derived Quot schemes, Lagrangian Foliations, and categorical Donaldson-Thomas invariants
papers.abstract:
We develop a derived-geometric framework for Donaldson--Thomas invariants in semistable Calabi--Yau threefold degenerations. Derived restriction from the two smooth components of the central fiber to their common anticanonical divisor is Lagrangian. We give explicit universal-family diagrams for this structure, compare the deformation complexes with perfect complexes on the singular union, and construct the fourfold duality using a canonical bundle pulled back from the base. On specified Quot presentations we describe the real Lagrangian foliation and its shifted potential.
  We formulate proper-completion and cohomological-comparison conjectures for sheaves arising from sections of an extending line bundle. Their specialization is described by oriented two-sided bar complexes and a finite Gauss--Manin system.

papers.title: Density coexistence for hard spheres with a long-range attractive pair interaction
papers.abstract: We prove low-temperature density coexistence for identical hard disks or hard spheres with a smooth, nonnegative, finite-range attractive Kac pair kernel. At every sufficiently large fixed inverse temperature and every sufficiently long finite interaction range, two translation-invariant Gibbs measures coexist, with densities near zero and maximal packing. The pressure is therefore nondifferentiable in chemical potential. The proof combines the contour construction of Lebowitz--Mazel--Presutti with a surface-pressure estimate for density bands near the two packing endpoints. A packing bound controls the fine density profile; centering the interaction makes its residual boundary contribution quadratic in the band width. Compatible near-packed configurations and conditional entropy then control the hard-core boundary contribution. These estimates allow the dense restricted ensemble to retain positional order and long-range correlations.

papers.title: Density functionals for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We develop a density-functional theory for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian of nonrelativistic quantum electrodynamics in the spirit of the convex-analytic formulation of Lieb. We consider finitely many electrons, subject to external scalar and vector potentials, coupled to the full continuum of massless transverse photons with an ultraviolet cutoff. The natural basic variables are the standard electron density and a combined current density, the sum of the paramagnetic current density and a field-induced current density generated by the quantized vector potential. We prove representability results for these density-current pairs and show that the mixed-state constrained-search functional attains its infimum and coincides with the Lieb functional obtained by convex conjugation. Since arbitrarily soft photons purify mixed states at a negligible energy cost without changing their density and combined current density, the pure-state Levy-Lieb functional equals the Lieb functional and is therefore convex, even though its infimum need not be attained. In addition, we establish the zero-coupling limit, which recovers the mixed-state Vignale-Rasolt functional of current-density-functional theory. Finally, we consider the long-wavelength (dipole) limit and show that the limiting functional can be written as a constrained search for the well-known length-gauge dipole Hamiltonian.

papers.title: Derived tame monomial algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite-dimensional connected monomial algebra over an algebraically closed field is derived tame if and only if every finite connected convex subcategory of its universal cover has non-negative Euler form. Derived tameness is also equivalent to tameness of its repetitive category and trivial extension. For one-cycle algebras, this condition is equivalent to the non-negativity on $\mathbb R$ of $|Q_0|$ explicitly computable polynomials in $\mathbb Q[t]$. This gives a finite algorithm for deciding derived tameness. We also construct an infinite family of derived-tame one-cycle string algebras with minimal cubic relations, no two of which are derived equivalent.

papers.title: Disconnected Stab(X) and infinitely many braid group orbits
papers.abstract: We show that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions Stab(Y) on a very general quintic threefold Y has infinitely many connected components. Using similar methods, we also prove that for a particular smooth projective (weak Fano) threefold X the braid group action on the set of full exceptional collections in Dscr^b(X) has infinitely many orbits, in particular, it is not transitive. This provides a counterexample to a conjecture of Bondal and Polishchuk from 1993. The conjecture was first disproved by Chang, Haiden, and Schroll, who constructed a family of partially wrapped Fukaya categories for which the transitivity fails. However, no counterexample of the form Dscr^b(X) for X a smooth projective variety was previously known. In addition, we show that Stab(X) also has infinitely many connected components. These are the first known examples of a smooth projective varieties whose spaces of Bridgeland stability conditions are disconnected.

papers.title: Disconnectedness of stability manifolds and their geometric loci, and separation of braid orbits of semiorthogonal decompositions
papers.abstract: This paper proves that the Bridgeland stability manifold $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ has infinitely many connected components for general quintic threefolds, other general complete intersection Calabi--Yau threefolds, certain odd-dimensional Calabi--Yau varieties, and certain rational weak Fano varieties. Moreover, we show that the geometric locus $\mathrm{Stab}^{\mathrm{geo}}(X)$ meets distinct connected components of $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ for general quintic threefolds and their products with varieties with finite Albanese morphisms, which gives examples in any dimension at least three. For the weak Fano examples, we also construct semiorthogonal decompositions in infinitely many braid group orbits. The proof is an extension of Nordskova's argument to families, using semilinear autoequivalences and absolute Galois actions on geometric generic fibers to permute mutually orthogonal spherical objects. Then, we specialize the separation to closed fibers. In our examples, the spherical objects are constructed from rigid rational curves or spinor bundles on quadrics.

papers.title: Distinction and quadratic base change for regular supercuspidal representations
papers.abstract: In this article, we study Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations based on the machinery developed by Hakim and Murnaghan to study distinguished representations, and the fundamental work of Kaletha on parameterization of regular supercuspidal representations. For regular supercuspidal representations, we give some new interpretations of the numerical quantities appearing in Prasad's formula, and reduce the proof to the case of tori. The proof of Prasad's conjecture then reduces to a comparison of various quadratic characters appearing naturally in the above process. We also have some new observations on these characters and study the relation between them in detail. For some particular examples, we show the coincidence of these characters, which gives a new purely local proof of Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of these groups. We also prove Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of G(E), when E/F is unramified and G is a general tamely ramified quasi-split reductive group.

papers.title: Equality of the Mirković–Vilonen and theta bases
papers.abstract: We prove Kamnitzer's ICM 2022 conjecture that the Mirković–Vilonen and theta bases coincide.

papers.title: Equivariant Ehrhart series for rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes
papers.abstract:
Equivariant Ehrhart theory was introduced by Stapledon (2011) and has since been extensively studied. A central question is whether the numerator in a certain rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series is both a polynomial and effective.
  In this paper, we propose a modification of the denominator in the rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series of rational polytopes. For rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes whose vertices have coordinates that are reciprocals of integers, we show that the resulting numerator is a polynomial and is effective. As an application of our results, we compute the equivariant series of the characteristic quasi-polynomials of root systems.

papers.title: Every real primitive Dirichlet L-function has de Bruijn–Newman constant at most 9/32: a kernel-checked proof in Lean 4
papers.abstract: Let χ be a real primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N ≥ 3 and parity k ∈ {0,1}. Let Λ(s,χ) = (N/π)^{(s+k)/2} Γ((s+k)/2) L(s,χ) be its completed L-function, and let H^χ_t(z) = ∫_0^∞ e^{tu²} Φ_χ(u) cos(zu) du be the de Bruijn–Newman heat flow of Λ(·,χ), normalised so that H^χ_0(z) = (1/8) Λ(1/2 + iz/2, χ). We give a proof, checked by the Lean 4 kernel, that for every such χ and every t ≥ 9/32 all zeros of H^χ_t are real. Equivalently, the generalised de Bruijn–Newman constant satisfies Λ_χ ≤ 9/32. The mathematics is not new, and we say exactly whose it is. De Bruijn's strip-contraction theorem (1950) gives Λ_χ ≤ D²/2 whenever the zeros of H^χ_0 lie in |Im z| ≤ D. Freire, González-Riquelme, Muñoz, Poblete and Salinas observed (arXiv:2610.27343, Remarks 3.1 and 3.4) that the zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for Dirichlet L-functions asserted by OpenAI would give D = 3/4, and hence Λ_χ ≤ 9/32. What this paper adds is a complete formal proof of that composition. For conductors up to 400, FGMPS's unconditional bounds are stronger for 136 of the 242 characters; what is new is that 9/32, for every conductor, is a kernel-checked theorem. OpenAI's half-plane enters as their own kernel-checked Lean theorem. Every other step is proved in Lean on top of Mathlib: de Bruijn's theorem for a general class of kernels, the identification of the theta integral with Mathlib's completed L-function, and Gauss's sign theorem for real primitive characters. The final theorem depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. In local, unsandboxed replays five checkers accept it: Lean's kernel (run twice), nanoda, and the con-leche/con-ron pair. All five reject a deliberately unsound control. A sandboxed Comparator run against a separately written challenge also accepts it. That run was made by another agent session, and the auditor reproduced its solution export byte for byte. The result rests on OpenAI's Lean proof, whose accompanying manuscript is unrefereed. It is not progress on the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis, which is the statement Λ_χ ≤ 0. A short, separable section records two companion results for ζ that use no OpenAI code, Λ ≤ 225/512 and ψ(x) = x + O_ε(x^{31/32+ε}), both from Cureton and Thorner's half-plane Re s > 31/32. Code, verification records and archive: https://github.com/DrMurphyIsIn/real-dirichlet-dbn-lean (release v1.0.0); DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23840082.

papers.title: Exchange graphs and $g$-vectors of surface rigid algebras
papers.abstract: We classify the connected components of support $\tau$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected if and only if the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules, and has Cartan rank one. In this case, it has exactly two connected components. For every nonzero $\tau$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra, the graph of $\tau$-tilting completions is connected. More generally, we classify the completion components for an arbitrary surface rigid algebra and a fixed $\tau$-rigid pair. For partial tagged triangulations with all endpoints at punctures, we express the Cartan matrix and $g$-vectors by signed endpoint data. We prove that $\tau$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates. Trees give type A, and a criterion on the original partial tagged triangulation distinguishes types D and C in the unicyclic case.

papers.title: Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules
papers.abstract: For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin. As an application, a holonomic binomial $D$-module is regular holonomic if and only if there are no tropical jumps along any coordinate subspace.

papers.title: Functorial Analysis of Group-Alphabet Cellular Automata
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $n\in\mathbb N$. We consider one-dimensional cellular automata of length $n$ over the alphabet $G$, with periodic boundary conditions and with local rules $\phi$ given by words. We construct a functor $F$ from $\mathbf{Grp}$, the category of groups (or any similar algebraic structure), to the category of pointed digraphs, and show its faithfulness. We introduce the image category $\mathcal C_{n,\phi}$ of state transition graphs of all such group-alphabet cellular automata, and show $F$ is an equivalence onto this category. Consequently we investigate the translation of categorical structures in $\mathbf{Grp}$ in terms of automata, and give examples of how standard methods of homological algebra may now be applied to automata. Additionally, a graph-theoretical construction of the product in $\mathcal C_{n,\phi}$ is given, together with a formula for cycle lengths and multiplicities in this product. When $G$ is abelian, further structural properties of state transition graphs follow, and we contrast these results with non-abelian counterexamples.

papers.title: Grassmannians of absolute Banach-Colmez Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce Grassmannians of absolute Banach--Colmez spaces and prove the $k$-Grassmannian is perfectoid if and only if the space has slope $< 1/k$. For $d=1$, this proves a conjecture of Hansen--Mann. The key ingredient is a Pl\"{u}cker morphism, which realizes the $k$-Grassmannian of a slope $d/n$ space as a Zariski closed subspace of the projectivization of a slope $kd/n$ space. We also introduce a general method to construct invariant elements in perfectoid Tate--Huber pairs, and use this to prove absolute Banach--Colmez spaces of slope $<1$ have perfectoid projectivizations. As applications, we establish vanishing bounds for Scholze's mod $p$ Jacquet--Langlands functor on parabolic inductions, and also prove its vanishing in the top degree on every infinite-dimensional non-supersingular irreducible representation.

papers.title: Haagerup vertex operator algebras at central charge eight
papers.abstract: Evans and Gannon showed that a positive vertex operator algebra of central charge eight whose representation category is the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category has one of two character vectors, with six or nineteen currents. Call such an algebra, if strongly rational, a Haagerup algebra. We prove that a Haagerup algebra $U$ has six currents, that $U_1 \cong \mathfrak{sl}_2 \oplus \mathfrak{sl}_2$ embeds into $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$ in one of two explicit ways, with levels $(1,39)$ or $(3,13)$, and we determine the lowest weight spaces of its modules and $U_2$ as $U_1$-modules. For the levels $(3,13)$, $U_2$ is one of four Galois conjugate subspaces, and the algebra it generates is unitary, $C_2$-cofinite and isomorphic to the algebra constructed by Jiao; for the levels $(1,39)$, $U$ contains the algebra announced by Riesen. The associated lattice of $U$ is that of the form $x^2+xy+10y^2$, resp.\ $3x^2+3xy+4y^2$, the two classes of the principal genus of discriminant $-39$. Exchanging them in the decomposition of $U$ over its Heisenberg commutant gives a Haagerup algebra $U^\natural$ of the other levels, and $U \mapsto U^\natural$ is a bijection between the isomorphism classes of the two cases. Consequently, if either explicit algebra of Jiao or Riesen is positive and strongly rational with representation category braided equivalent to $Z(\cal H_3)$, there are exactly two Haagerup algebras up to isomorphism, forming a single hyperbolic genus. The explicit algebras of Jiao and Riesen have rational forms. The proofs combine exact trace relations given by vector-valued modular forms, exact computations in a model of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$, and genera of vertex operator algebras.

papers.title: Haiman's conjecture for n <= 10: Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity of monomial immanants
papers.abstract:
Haiman conjectured that for every partition $\lambda\vdash n$ and every $w\in S_n$ the polynomial $c_{\lambda,w}(q)$, a monomial character of the Hecke algebra evaluated at the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, has non-negative integer coefficients and is symmetric and unimodal, and he verified this by computer for $n\le7$. We verify it for every $n\le10$. A stability lemma reduces the statement to $n=10$, which we settle by an exact computation that stores only the 1,252,173,030 pairs $(x,w)$ in $S_{10}$ with $x$ maximal in its double coset for the descent sets of $w$, and takes the traces of the standard basis from the class polynomials of Geck and Pfeiffer. Every stored Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial agrees with du Cloux's Coxeter3, and the coefficients pass several independent checks, including a comparison at all 16,796 codominant $w$ with chromatic quasisymmetric functions computed from colourings.
  Consequently, for $n\le10$ every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants, Stembridge's monomial immanant conjecture holds, and a class-function immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices if and only if it is non-negative at the block matrices $J_\mu$. We use this to describe the order of normalised irreducible-character immanants on totally non-negative matrices for $n\le10$, and to prove Pate's inequalities there. On the full span of permutation monomials we give a Newton-polytope criterion for the coefficient of $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ to be non-negative throughout the totally non-negative cone, show that for $n=4,5$ this happens exactly when $X_w$ is smooth, and check by exact computation for $n\le10$ the proof of this for all $n$ given in a companion paper.

papers.title: Holomorphic functions and hulls of Matsuki-dual orbits of $SU(p,q)$ in complex Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Let $G_0$ be a real form of a complex semisimple group acting on a flag manifold $Z$, with maximal compact subgroup $K_0$ and its complexification $K$. Matsuki duality pairs each $G_0$-orbit $\gamma$ with a $K$-orbit $\kappa$, and $M=\kappa\cap\gamma$ is a compact $K_0$-orbit. For lower-dimensional $\gamma$, $M$ is a compact CR manifold, and we ask which functions are holomorphic near $M$ and what its holomorphic hull is. In general, we show that $K_0$-finite holomorphic functions near $M$ are regular functions on $K$-orbits, and that $M$ carries non-constant holomorphic germs if some $K$-stable prime divisor of $Z$ misses $\kappa$, and, under a connectedness hypothesis, only constants otherwise. For $G_0=SU(p,q)$ acting on any Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_k(\mathbb{C}^{p+q})$ we give a complete answer. Holomorphic functions near $M$ are constant unless $M$ is of holomorphic type: $k\in\{p,q\}$ and $M$ lies in the Harish-Chandra chart of the bounded symmetric domain $\mathcal{D}$. Then $M$ is the manifold of rank-$c$ partial isometries, and a holomorphic hull of $M$ is $\overline{\mathcal{D}}\cap\{\mathrm{rank}\le c\}$. This agrees with the polynomial hull of Kaup and Zaitsev except in one totally real case, where it is strictly smaller because $\det^{-1}$ is holomorphic near $U(p)$. The same dichotomy decides when global CR functions on $M$ are constant and when holomorphic sections of line bundles near $M$ are global; its exceptions differ from the Gindikin-Matsuki exceptions for cycle spaces, except at the base point of $\mathcal{D}$. This settles the descent question left open in earlier work with K. Shabbir on rank-one orbits. We also determine which $K$-orbits carry non-constant regular functions, prove constancy via chains of rational curves for small $c$, and compute Levi forms in examples.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$
papers.abstract: Bryan, Oberdieck, Pandharipande and Yin predicted the number of hyperelliptic curves on general abelian surfaces under a transversality condition. Some of the numbers have already been confirmed. In this paper we construct singular hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ polarised abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$ confirming a few predicted numbers, namely of (geometric) genus $g=d$ and of geometric genus $k+3$ on $(1,2k)$ and $(1,2k+1)$ polarised surfaces. Moreover, we have found that all genus 7 hyperelliptic curves on general $(1,8)$ polarised surfaces are double coverings of curves locally embedded into $(1,4)$ polarised surfaces. More interestingly, there is a unique genus 9 hyperelliptic curve (up to translation) locally embedded into a general $(1,12)$ polarised surface and it is a Klein covering of a curve locally embedded into a $(1,3)$ polarised surface.

papers.title: Illumination of complex 1-unconditional convex bodies
papers.abstract: We study ordinary and fractional illumination of complex $1$-unconditional convex bodies. In every complex dimension $n$ we give an explicit ordinary bound asymptotic to $3^{n+1}/\sqrt{\pi n}$, and prove $\ill^*(K)\le b_*^n$ and $\ill(K)=O(n\log(n+1)b_*^n)$, where $b_*=2.4805534697\ldots$ is defined by an explicit scalar equation. For normalized non-polydiscs in dimensions two, three and four, the sharp ordinary bounds are $6$, $14$ and $30$. More generally, a full coordinate $(n-1)$-polydisc gives the sharp bound $2^{n+1}-2$ in every dimension $n\ge2$. In dimension two we prove the fractional bound $4$ and classify equality by the two maximal supporting coefficients at the coordinate axes. If every extreme point has all coordinates nonzero, we obtain the fractional bound $2^n$, with equality exactly for the polydisc, and a quantitative strict bound otherwise. Appendices give the exact sizes of simultaneous illuminating families in dimensions one through five, the exact finite verification used in dimension four, and a numerical comparison of the general estimates through dimension $100$.

papers.title: Illumination of several families of complex convex bodies
papers.abstract: We determine ordinary and fractional illumination numbers for complex Hanner bodies and for bodies obtained as convex hulls of coordinate polydiscs indexed by the maximal independent sets of a graph. The formulas are sums over coordinate supports. For Hanner bodies we classify all equality cases in the ordinary and fractional dimension bounds, including the sharp ordinary bound for non-polydiscs. For graph bodies, fractional equality $2^n$ occurs exactly when the graph is a disjoint union of isolated vertices and edges; a vertex of degree at least two gives the strict bound $3\cdot2^{n-2}$. We also prove the fractional bound $2^n$ for bodies defined by nondecreasing submodular constraints on coordinate moduli. For finite systems of positive weighted inequalities satisfying an explicit condition on tight sets, we obtain the same fractional bound and an ordinary bound of $(2+o(1))n\log n\,2^n$, together with an explicit estimate in every dimension. This includes bounded systems on laminar families with arbitrary positive coefficients. We conclude with a conjectural classification of fractional equality for normalized complex $1$-unconditional bodies.

papers.title: Improved and sharp bounds for illumination
papers.abstract: We prove improved ordinary illumination bounds and exact ordinary and fractional values for several classes of convex bodies. Every full-dimensional complex zonotope in $\C^2$ has illumination number five, except complex affine images of the bidisc, whose number is seven. For complex $1$-symmetric non-polydiscs in $\C^3$, an explicit construction gives twelve illuminating directions. For real $1$-symmetric non-cubes in $\R^n$, connected domination in the cube graph gives the upper bound $2^{n-1}+\gamma_c(Q_{n-1})+n-1 =2^{n-1}(1+(1+o(1))/n)$; an explicit family has illumination number $2^{n-1}$. We also give a product boundary measure proving fractional lower bounds $2^n$ for bodies between specified inner and outer bodies, and attain these bounds along Minkowski interpolations with a positive inner summand. Finally, the least size $U_n$ of a single family illuminating every normalized complex $1$-unconditional body satisfies $U_n\sim3^{n+1}/\sqrt{\pi n}$.

papers.title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
papers.abstract: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.

papers.title: Integral Hodge structures and atoms of fourfolds
papers.abstract: Following the recent work by OpenAI on the irrationality of very general cubic fourfolds in Hassett divisors, we prove some compatibility of Iritani's blow-up formula with the classical blow-up decomposition of integral Hodge structures. As a consequence, we express OpenAI's birational invariant in terms of the theory of atoms developped by Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu. We also show that, for every smooth complex rational cubic fourfold, the primitive cohomology is isometric as an integral Hodge structure to the twisted middle cohomology of a K3 surface and we prove irrationality of the very general Verra fourfold.

papers.title: Irreducible representations of tree automorphism groups into Pontryagin spaces
papers.abstract: Let G = Aut(T) be the automorphism group of a regular tree T. We study continuous irreducible representations of G that preserve a continuous strongly nondegenerate sesquilinear form of finite index on a Hilbert space. These are already classified for index 0 (unitary case) and for index 1. We show that there are no more representations for index > 1, which completes the classification.

papers.title: Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields
papers.abstract: We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Th\'el\`ene, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.

papers.title: Jordan-H\"older theory for complementary polyhedra and moduli of parahoric Higgs torsors
papers.abstract: We extend Behrend's theory of complementary polyhedra to include Jordan-H\"older theory by introducing the notion of Jordan-H\"older facets. As a consequence, we can construct Jordan-H\"older parabolic subgroup schemes for reductive group schemes over a smooth projective curve. We use these results to provide a uniform approach to describing Jordan-H\"older filtrations and S-equivalence of moduli stacks of semistable bundles, including vector bundles, principal bundles, parabolic bundles, parahoric torsors, and parahoric Higgs torsors, following Zhang. We explicitly give a description of Jordan-H\"older filtrations and S-equivalence in the semistable locus of parahoric torsors and parahoric Higgs torsors, coming from their good moduli spaces, as constructed by Alper-Halpern-Leistner-Heinloth and R\'ega. This application uses the Rees construction, as given by Heinloth, to identify filtrations of moduli stacks of parahoric torsors with reductions of parahoric torsors to parabolic subgroups, inducing Jordan-H\"older stratifications of the moduli stacks.

papers.title: Kloosterman Sums and Pl\"ucker Height Zeta Functions
papers.abstract: We establish nontrivial bounds for Kloosterman sums over $p$-adic fields associated with the longest Weyl element on arbitrary split reductive groups, at arbitrary level. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions (of Whittaker models) for all such groups.

papers.title: Lower bounds for the quantum permanent
papers.abstract: Griffiths's 1969 conjecture on the positivity of Schur forms reduces to the positivity of the quantum permanent $\Phi_n$ on positive bistochastic maps. This conjecture was refuted by Du with a map for which $\Phi_9<0$. Therefore, we ask: how negative can $\Phi_n$ be? We prove a lower bound $\Phi_n\ge-3n/(3n^2+20n+103)$ (for $n\ge 8$), and an asymptotically stronger bound $\Phi_n\ge-1/n+(3e^2-7-o(1))\log n/n^2$. The key to our bounds is the orbital polynomial of the map, which turns $\Phi_n$ into a linear function of a distribution on partitions and positivity into linear constraints. We also construct explicit maps for $n=8, 9$ that improve on Du's example. Finally, if $d_*\in\{4,\ldots,8\}$ is the first dimension for which $\Phi_n<0$, the minimum $\mu_n$ of $\Phi_n$ over positive bistochastic maps satisfies $-\mu_n=\Omega(n^{-d_*})$; we conjecture the matching order $-\mu_n=O(n^{-d_*})$.

papers.title: Minimal recurrences for binomial power sums
papers.abstract: For every positive integer $r$, we prove that the least order of a polynomial-coefficient recurrence for $F_r(n)=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom nk^r$ is $\lfloor(r+1)/2\rfloor$. This establishes the unrestricted minimal-order assertion arising from Franel's work of 1894--1895. We also determine the least order $\lfloor r/2\rfloor$, for $r\geq2$, of the alternating sums $(-1)^n\sum_{k=0}^{2n}(-1)^k\binom{2n}{k}^r$. The lower bounds follow from real moment representations: every nonzero singularity of the representing measure forces a root of the leading characteristic polynomial of the recurrence. A common reflection argument gives telescoping recurrences attaining both bounds. For the ordinary sums, we combine the deformation of Straub and Zudilin with a shifted prime-power congruence to prove that the minimal shift operator is irreducible over $\C(n)$.

papers.title: Monotonicity of Turán-ratios of symmetric polynomials
