papers.abstract: We study the Turán-ratio $S_{\lambda,i}(x)^2/(S_{\lambda,i-1}(x)S_{\lambda,i+1}(x))$, where $S_{\lambda,i}(x):=s_\lambda(1^{[n-i]},x^{[i]})$, and $s_\lambda$ is the Schur polynomial in $n$ variables (indexed by partition $\lambda$) with $i$ arguments equal to $x$ and $n-i$ of them equal to $1$. Specifically, we prove that this Turán-ratio is strictly increasing for $x>1$ and $1\le i<n$ (unless all $n$ padded parts of $\lambda$ are equal, then it is identically one). For one-row shapes, our result answers a question of Ait-Haddou about complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials. For this case, we also offer a second proof through the zeros of Meixner polynomials that gives an explicit positive formula for the logarithmic derivative. We conclude with a Turán-ratio conjecture for Macdonald polynomials.

papers.title: Noncommutative Cauchy Bound and Noncommutative Montel Bound for Roots of Polynomials
papers.abstract: In 1829, Cauchy derived an upper bound for every root of a complex polynomial using the maximum of the absolute values of the coefficients. In 1931, Montel derived an upper bound using the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients. We derive noncommutative versions of the Cauchy and Montel bounds.

papers.title: Nonlinear Maps Between Irreducible Representations in Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Equivariant linear maps cannot mix non-isomorphic irreducible representations, whereas nonlinear activations can. We develop a degree-resolved version of this nonlinear interaction picture and use the resulting block inventory to construct Specht Triple, a residual on unordered graph triples. On a synthetic structural benchmark with a frozen GIN backbone, Specht Triple reduces aggregate standardised test MSE by 11.05% relative to a parameter-matched Projector Control using the same irreducible projectors and complete linear equivariant space. The results support irreducible decomposition as an inductive bias for nonlinear higher-order equivariant processing.

papers.title: Numerical Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for rank-three matroids
papers.abstract: We prove the numerical Kawamata--Viehweg conjecture for every matroid of rank three: the Euler characteristic of the inverse of an integral big and nef line bundle class is nonnegative. The proof reduces the conjecture to an inequality for a stone game.

papers.title: On a Family of Counterexamples to Richard Guy's Mex Sequence Problem
papers.abstract: We give a family of counterexamples to Richard Guy's problem E27 with initial terms of length five adding onto the recent example of length eight. Additionally, we prove that for length one, one always has a ultimately periodic sequence. Lastly we pose a problem regarding the notion of a zth mex sequence.

papers.title: On Boundary State Screening via Solitons
papers.abstract: We present a coarse classification scheme for the boundary data of massive QFTs based on transitions of boundary states via soliton / kink profiles. Starting from the lattice of boundary states, we introduce the boundary screening group $\mathbb{B}$: the equivalence classes of boundary states which cannot be connected by such transitions. In string theory backgrounds which geometrically engineer an interacting QFT in the target space, $\mathbb{B}$ computes the worldsheet analog of the target space defect group $\mathbb{D}$. When $\mathbb{B}$ is non-zero, it provides a diagnostic for having a target space with non-normalizable modes. For interfaces between QFTs, similar considerations imply the existence of a non-trivial conserved charge associated with soliton absorption / transmission, which means that the interface cannot fully dissolve / disappear. Similar considerations hold for junctions of QFTs, which in the special case of string worldsheet CFTs translate to junctions of string theories. We illustrate these general considerations with a number of non-geometric 2D $\mathcal{N} = (2,2)$ Landau-Ginzburg models, as well as their natural lifts to 4D $\mathcal{N} = 1$ Wess-Zumino models.

papers.title: On majorization inequalities for normalized Jack and Macdonald polynomials
papers.abstract: We study the inequality $P_\lambda(x;q,t)/P_\lambda(1^n;q,t)\geq P_\mu(x;q,t)/P_\mu(1^n;q,t)$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}^n$ whenever the partition $\lambda$ majorizes $\mu$; Sra suggested it in 2015, and Chen, Khare and Sahi stated it as a conjecture in 2025. We prove the Jack case for every $n$ from Sun's positive Gelfand–Tsetlin integral and the Dixon–Anderson recursion. For Macdonald polynomials we prove the case $n=2$, the covers $(d)\succeq(d-1,1)$ for every $n$ when $t\leq q$, and, by exact certificates, the case $n=3$ with $|\lambda|\leq 8$. The HCIZ mechanism behind the Jack proof has no direct finite-$q$ analogue: at two explicit pairs $(q,t)$, no positive representation of the normalized ratio has a kernel multiplicative in $\lambda$, and normalizing at the principal specialization $t^\delta$ instead fails the inequality.

papers.title: On Problem 5 of Vitorino and Vukusic: $\sup_{k\ge 0} B(2^k\alpha)\ge 12$
papers.abstract: For an irrational $\alpha$ let $B(\alpha)=\limsup_n a_n(\alpha)$ be the upper limit of its partial quotients. Vitorino and Vukusic proved $\sup_{k\ge 0}B(2^k\alpha)\ge 5$ for every irrational $\alpha$ and asked, as their Problem 5, for an improvement. We prove $\sup_{k\ge 0}B(2^k\alpha)\ge 12$. The proof is a finite computation organised around an invariant $N(C)$: the least number of doubling levels at which the recurrent kernel of a synchronous product of Raney transducers becomes a finite union of pure cycles. We show that $N(C)$ is intrinsic, that $N(C)<\infty$ for every $C$ would imply the $2$-adic Littlewood conjecture, and that $N(C)=\infty$ is equivalent to a rigidity failure; we compute $N(C)=1,1,3,5,5,8,15,21,29,30,31$ for $C=1,\dots,11$. In the language of Badziahin's set LMad this settles a level-bounded form of his Problem B for $C\le 11$. The cycles which survive are ideal classes of discriminant $D\equiv 1 \pmod 8$ whose whole $\mathfrak{p}_2$-orbit has partial quotients at most $C$; we list them, and check the lists by an independent arithmetic route, in both directions for $D\le 10^5$. The result concerns the upper limit $B$ only. On the side of the supremum $M$ it gives $\sup_k M(2^k\alpha)\ge 12$, which is weaker than what is known: Vitorino and Vukusic prove $15$, and Badziahin's bound $1/25$ yields $24$. Two self-contained Python files, without external dependency, reproduce the table and the lists of discriminants; the table up to $C=8$ takes about fourteen seconds.

papers.title: On the classifying space of a Morse flow category
papers.abstract: We show that the classifying space of the flow category of a \emph{tame} Morse function on a smooth, closed manifold $M$ recovers the homotopy type of $M$, thereby addressing a claim in a preprint of Cohen--Jones--Segal. The tameness assumption is that the compactified moduli spaces of broken gradient trajectories are locally contractible, ensuring the flow category is topologically well-behaved. We construct a Morse function and Riemannian metric on $S^2\times S^1$ for which the associated flow category fails to recover the correct homotopy type, showing that the tameness hypothesis is crucial. Together, these results clarify the extent to which transversality assumptions can be relaxed so that the flow category models the homotopy type of the underlying manifold.

papers.title: On the generic case of Jiang's conjecture
papers.abstract: Jiang's conjecture predicts that if $\pi$ is a generic representation of a quasi-split $p$-adic group, then the $L$-parameter of the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution of $\pi$ must be trivial on $\mathrm{SL}_2$. In this paper, we prove this statement for a general quasi-split group under certain assumptions on the conjectural local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: On the Jacobian algebras of Ziegler pairs of plane arrangements
papers.abstract: We consider a Ziegler pair of plane arrangements, that is two plane arrangements $\mathcal{A}:f=0$ and $\mathcal{A}':f'=0$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^3$, such that the intersection lattices $L(\mathcal{A})$ and $L(\mathcal{A}')$ are isomorphic, but the Betti numbers of the minimal resolutions of their Jacobian algebras are not the same. We introduce several properties for such pairs and relate them to cones over Ziegler pairs of line arrangements in $\mathbb{P}^2$.

papers.title: On the maximality conjecture for quantum permutation groups
papers.abstract: A well-known conjecture, central in quantum permutation group theory, and going back to around 2006, states that $S_N\subset S_N^+$ is maximal. We revisit here this conjecture, and related questions, 20 years after, with 2026 knowledge and tools.

papers.title: On the tensor-triangular geometry of isotropic motives
papers.abstract: We investigate the tensor-triangular geometry of the categories of isotropic Tate motives, isotropic Artin motives and isotropic Artin--Tate motives. In particular, we study the categories $DTM_{gm}(k/k;\mathbb{F}_2)$, $DAM_{gm}(k/k;\mathbb{F}_2)$ and $DATM_{gm}(k/k;\mathbb{F}_2)$ where $k$ is a flexible field and we fix $\mathbb{F}_2$-coefficients. In this case, we prove their Balmer spectra are singletons. The proof of this relies on the fact that the categories in question are generated by objects whose morphisms are `nilpotent enough.' Furthermore, we investigate their homological spectra, and verify Balmer's Nerves of Steel conjecture in these cases by showing these spaces are also singletons, and we give an explicit description of the homological primes. We also investigate stratification, and we conclude by studying generation properties of these categories -- the latter results we see also apply to global (i.e. non-isotropic) motives.

papers.title: On unitary representations of $p$-adic $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}$ and $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ of purely bad parity
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$ or split $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$ over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We classify the irreducible unitary representations of $G$ of purely bad parity: such a representation is unitary if and only if it is of Arthur type, except for one additional family when $G=\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$. In particular, we confirm the remaining case of Ciubotaru's conjecture for $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$, namely that every unitary unipotent representation with integral infinitesimal parameter is of Arthur type.

papers.title: Open WDVV equations and $\bigvee$-systems
papers.abstract: The idea of a $\bigvee$-system was introduced by Veselov in the study of rational solutions of the WDVV equations of associativity. These are algebraic/geometric conditions on the set of covectors that appear in rational solutions to the WDVV equations. Here, this idea is generalized to open WDVV equations, which are an additional set of PDEs originating from open Gromow-Witten Theory. We develop -- for rank-one extensions -- algebraic/geometric conditions on the covectors that supplement the $\bigvee$-system to give rational solutions to the open WDVV equations. Examples, and the relation to superpotentials and to Dubrovin almost-duality, are given.

papers.title: Period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$
papers.abstract: Using the modular symbol approach, we prove the rationality and period relations for certain critical values of Rankin-Selberg L-functions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$ over any number field that contains a CM field.

papers.title: Periodic Tunnel Systems: Reeb Graph Representations and Circular Max-Flow
papers.abstract: Inspired by the study of transport properties in materials science, we investigate the Reeb graph of a map \(f:X\to\Ss\), interpreting \(X\) as a periodic tunnel system in which transport takes place. The map \(f\) encodes a chosen periodic direction and induces a directed structure on the graph. Under constructibility, we establish a lifting result for directed paths that makes precise how the graph represents tunnel segments in \(X\). To turn this representation into a numerical transport descriptor, we equip the graph with cross-sectional capacities defined, in a Riemannian setting, by weighted Hausdorff-measure integrals. Under boundary regularity and Morse assumptions in dimension \(d\ge2\), we establish continuity over regular Reeb values and continuity of the total capacity across fibers. Taking edgewise infima gives the bottleneck capacities for a circular max-flow formulation, which measures flow through fibers of the map to the circle without choosing an arbitrary inlet or outlet. The resulting descriptor is computable by linear optimization and is related to minimum-cost circulations. For nonnegative real capacities, we prove that the max-flow value is invariant under periodic unrolling: the same descriptor is obtained whether the medium is modeled by a toroidal cell or by its periodic replication along the chosen direction. Simulations on periodic point clouds illustrate the construction and the effects of imposing source--target cuts.

papers.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, remixed
papers.abstract: For each endotrivial complex for a $p$-group arising from Bredon homology of a representation sphere, we construct $p$-local quasi-isomorphisms, called forerunners. These enable us to extend Balmer--Gallauer's results concerning the tensor-triangular geometry of permutation modules for elementary abelian $p$-groups to all $p$-groups. We construct an open cover of the Balmer spectrum under which all endotrivials are tt-line bundles, that is, every endotrivial is locally isomorphic to a shift of the tensor unit. We define a remixed permutation twisted cohomology ring for which the canonical comparison map from the Balmer spectrum to the homogeneous spectrum of the twisted cohomology ring is injective. If the twisted cohomology ring is Noetherian, the comparison map is an open immersion, and the open cover endows the Balmer spectrum with Dirac scheme structure. We prove Noetherianity holds for Dedekind groups and the dihedral group of order 8, and conjecture it holds for all $p$-groups.

papers.title: Positive polytopes and the full Fock–Goncharov conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the origin-interior form of the polytope criterion of Gross, Hacking, Keel and Kontsevich: over a field of characteristic zero, full Fock–Goncharov for a principal coefficient cluster variety is equivalent to the existence of a bounded full-dimensional positive polytope containing the origin in its interior. Replacing the interior condition by membership of the origin gives a false criterion.

papers.title: Projected stated (SL_n)-skein algebras and the Huang–Wang conjectures
papers.abstract: We prove Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6 of Min Huang and Zhihao Wang: the projected stated (SL_n)-skein algebra equals its quantum cluster and upper cluster algebras, and the specified exchangeable variables generate it over the frozen Laurent coefficient algebra. The results hold for triangulable unpunctured marked surfaces with at least two boundary marked points per connected component, over every coefficient domain and parameter in the conjectures.

papers.title: Push forwards of smooth measures on the unitary group in odd characteristic under the Chevalley map are almost bounded
papers.abstract:
In this paper we study analytic properties of the Chevalley map $p:\mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{c}$ where $\mathfrak{u}$ is the Lie algebra of a unitary group over a local field of odd characteristics. This map essentially sends a matrix to its characteristic polynomial.
  Our main result is that smooth compactly supported measures on $\mathfrak{u}$ are pushed by the Chevalley map to measures on $\mathfrak{c}$ with density functions in $L^q(\mathfrak{c})$ for all $q < \infty$. We also provide similar results for the Chevalley map attached to the unitary group.
  An important consequence is an odd characteristic analogue to results of Harish-Chandra stating the local integrability of the orbital integrals on the unitary group and its Lie algebra. Further possible applications to local integrability of characters of admissible representations of unitary groups over local fields of odd characteristic are also discussed.

papers.title: Quasi-projective dimensions over homological ring epimorphisms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study quasi-projective dimensions of modules over rings connected by homological ring epimorphisms. We establish several inequalities relating the quasi-projective dimensions over the source and target rings. As applications, we investigate the quasi-global dimension of triangular matrix rings and provide examples showing that the class of modules with finite quasi-projective dimension does not satisfy the 2-out-of-3 property in general.

papers.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
papers.abstract: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $\kappa$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tilde{\Delta}$). We prove that, for most toric surfaces and tangency orders, the invariant $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ is zero in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$. This is done by enumerating tropical curves with Block--G\"ottsche multiplicities. Additionally, we prove that, in many situations, the lower bound, given by the absolute value $|W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}|$ of $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$, for the number of oriented real rational curves is not sharp close to the tropical limit in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$.

papers.title: Rational limits in Markov–Euclid asymptotics
papers.abstract: We construct an infinite reduced mutation sequence for which all three logarithmic Markov–Euclid ratios converge to 9/10. This disproves the irrationality conjecture of Zhichao Chen and Zelin Jia (Conjecture 6.12).

papers.title: Relative Du Bois complexes over higher dimensional bases
papers.abstract: We extend the notion of the right relative Du Bois complex to a smooth base of arbitrary dimension. We further show that this complex satisfies base change in the sense of Kov\'acs--Taji, for flat families with strict higher Du Bois fibers, extending the result by Ning over a smooth curve.

papers.title: Relative homological algebra of filter modules
papers.abstract: Over an arbitrary ordered set we consider the class of filter modules, i.e. indicator modules of filters in the ordered set. We show that the induced exact structure of filter modules, the so-called filter exact structure, which has filter modules as relative projective modules, admits an explicit projectivization by the distributive lattice of filters. This allows the reduction of the projective-homological properties of the induced exact structure to the standard homological algebra of $k{\operatorname{Fil}(Q)}$, the incidence algebra of $k$-representations on the lattice of filters. In the case of finite join-semilattices, we leverage the combinatorial structure of the distributive lattice of filters to determine the standard global dimension of $k{\operatorname{Fil}(Q)}$. By virtue of projectivization we provide lower and upper bounds for the global dimension of the filter exact structure. Moreover, we call an ordered set filter-tiny if its relative injective modules one-to-one-correspond to the standard injective modules. We exploit relative derived functors to show that filter-tiny ordered sets do not admit relative injective prehulls if the relative global dimension is larger than 1. It is open to which classes of ordered sets $Q$ the filter-tininess condition applies, and what the relative injective modules are in the case of non-filter-tiny ordered sets.

papers.title: Riordan lattice paths counted by area
papers.abstract: We study Riordan paths enumerated by the area between the path and the axis. We show that the generating function satisfies a $q$-Riccati equation and can be written in a closed form as a ratio of basic hypergeometric series. The auxiliary series admits an algebraic representation as the motivic generating series of a symmetric two-node quiver. We obtain explicit formulas for the coefficients, the exponential asymptotics of the number of paths of given area, and a linear recurrence whose coefficients are signed counts of partitions into distinct parts. For a random path of area $n$ we obtain a joint Gaussian limit law for the numbers of returns, horizontal steps and up steps. The height is of order $\sqrt{\log n}$, and its distribution concentrates on two adjacent integers determined explicitly by $n$.

papers.title: Robin's Inequality at Colossally Abundant Numbers and Nicolas' Inequality at Their Largest Prime Factor
papers.abstract: Robin's criterion states that the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $\sigma(n) < e^{\gamma} \cdot n \cdot \log\log n$ for every $n > 5040$, and Nicolas' criterion states that it holds if and only if $c(q) = \log(q\#/\varphi(q\#)) - \gamma - \log\log\theta(q) > 0$ for every prime $q$, where $q\#$ is the primorial of $q$ and $\theta$ is the Chebyshev function. Let $N$ be a colossally abundant number, let $\xi(N)$ be the real number associated with $N$ by Nicolas, and let $q$ be the largest prime not exceeding $\xi(N)$. Writing $\Delta(N) = \log(\sigma(N)/N) - \gamma - \log\log\log N$, we prove without any hypothesis that, whenever $\log q \geq 31$, $1.353/(\sqrt{q} \log^{2} q) \leq \Delta(N) - c(q) + 2\sqrt{2}/(\sqrt{q} \log q) \leq 3.970/(\sqrt{q} \log^{2} q)$. Thus Robin's inequality at $N$ and Nicolas' inequality at $q$ differ by $2\sqrt{2}/(\sqrt{q} \log q)$ up to an explicit error of smaller order. As consequences, every colossally abundant counterexample to Robin's inequality yields a prime $q$ with $c(q) > 2.70/(\sqrt{q} \log q)$; conversely, every prime $q$ with $\log q \geq 31$ and $c(q) > 2\sqrt{2}(1 - 0.4787/\log q)/(\sqrt{q} \log q)$ yields a colossally abundant counterexample, so that Nicolas' oscillation theorem implies Robin's theorem on colossally abundant counterexamples; and under the Riemann Hypothesis every colossally abundant number with $\log q \geq 31$ satisfies $\Delta(N) < -0.654/(\sqrt{q} \log q)$, in accordance with the constant $2(\sqrt{2}-1)$ of Ramanujan's bound. For superabundant counterexamples, using the exponent bound of Nazardonyavi and Yakubovich, which gives $\log n \geq \psi(p_{k})$ for the largest prime factor $p_{k}$, we prove $c(p_{k}) > 0.9991/(\sqrt{p_{k}} \log p_{k})$, and we show that the least colossally abundant number not smaller than the least counterexample $n$ is itself a counterexample $N$ with $\log N - \log\xi(N) \leq \log n$.

papers.title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
papers.abstract: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(\mu)$ associated to a partition $\mu=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \kappa_\mu:=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]

papers.title: Shared Randomness and Normalization in One-Use Loop Communication
papers.abstract: We study a finite-message communication model defined by contracting one backward binary symmetric channel with one fixed, finite-dimensional forward quantum channel and then normalizing the resulting weights. The devices may share a finite classical seed that is independent of the message before normalization. The seed branches are mixed at the level of unnormalized weights, followed by a single normalization for each message. For M ≥ 2 messages, backward crossover probability 0 < p < 1/2, and forward channel Φ, we derive the exact worst-message success probability S_raw(Φ,p,M) = 2(1−p)/[M−(M−2)(1−2p)δ(Φ)], where δ(Φ) = max over input states ρ, σ of ½‖Φ(ρ)−Φ(σ)‖₁. The quantity δ is the established trace-distance contraction coefficient, not a new channel invariant. A cyclic construction with M seed values attains the bound. Crucially, normalization can make the posterior seed distribution message-dependent: the theorem does not describe an average of separately normalized branches or require success for every seed. We give an exact example separating these conventions. Matched depolarizing-qubit and classical binary symmetric forward channels consequently have equal optima in this resource model. The result is a restricted one-use optimization, not a physical backward-communication protocol or a general asymptotic capacity theorem.

papers.title: Sharp order-four sign regularity of a Jacobi theta kernel
papers.abstract: We prove that the Hankel kernel $\Phi(\sqrt{x+y})$, where $\Phi$ is the Jacobi theta kernel whose cosine transform is the Riemann $\Xi$-function, is strictly reverse-regular through order four. The order is sharp: an interval enclosure of the fifth Hankel–Wronskian at $t=10^{-2}$ shows failure at order five. The third-order condition is Csordas's conjecture that $s'^2-ss''$ is strictly log-concave for $s(t)=\Phi(\sqrt t)$. The proof reduces the kernel minors to Wronskian signs and establishes the signs by exact polynomial estimates for $t\ge1$ and interval arithmetic on $[0,1]$. The fourth-order sign also yields three positive iterates of $s\mapsto s'^2-ss''$, the triple Turán inequalities for the normalized Taylor coefficients of $\Xi$, and quartic integral inequalities for $\Xi$.

papers.title: Smith Algebra from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Tensor Product Branching via the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko Algebra
papers.abstract: Let $L_n$ be the finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $n$. We study the space of highest-weight vectors in $L_n\otimes L_m$ for the diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action. The extremal projector constructs these singular vectors and gives operators connecting the highest-weight lines in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition. We interpret these operators in the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko algebra of the diagonal pair $(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2, \mathfrak{sl}_2^{\mathrm{diag}})$. A rescaling of their quadratic relation yields the cubic Smith relation $[E,F]=2(H^3-cH)$. This cubic algebra is also known as a Higgs algebra in the physics literature. We express both the central parameter $c$ and the Smith Casimir in terms of the quadratic $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Casimir elements of the two tensor factors. The singular subspace becomes an irreducible Smith module of dimension $\min\{n,m\}+1$, with explicit formulas for the actions of the raising and lowering operators $E$ and $F$. Finally, comparison with finite-dimensional simple Smith modules gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a module to arise from this tensor-product construction.

papers.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
papers.abstract: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.

papers.title: The $p$-Bures–Wasserstein distance via $3\times3$ block matrices (with application to $p$-Bures–Wasserstein barycenters)
papers.abstract: We study the $p$-Bures–Wasserstein distance $D_p(A,B)=(\mathrm{tr}\,A^p+\mathrm{tr}\,B^p-2\|A^{1/2}B^{1/2}\|_p^p)^{1/2}$ on positive semidefinite matrices; it equals the Bures–Wasserstein distance for $p=1$, and the Hilbert–Schmidt distance for $p=2$. We prove that $D_p$ is a metric for every $1\le p\le2$, by proving a stronger 2014 conjecture of Lin and van den Driessche on $3\times3$ block matrices. Our main tool is a partition inequality for Schatten norms, proved by complex interpolation. We also characterize Fréchet means for $D_p$ by a fixed-point equation and prove geometric convergence of the associated iteration.

papers.title: The $q$-Foulkes problem I: A fusion inequality for Macdonald plethysms
papers.abstract: We prove that the plethysm $H_m[\widetilde H_\mu]$ of a Macdonald polynomial by the Hall–Littlewood polynomial $H_m$ lies above the Macdonald polynomial $\widetilde H_{m\mu}$ obtained by fusing $m$ copies of $\widetilde H_\mu$. More specifically, the quotient $(H_m[\widetilde H_\mu]-\widetilde H_{m\mu})/(1-q^m)$ is Schur positive with coefficients in $\mathbb N[q,t]$, and it is the character of an explicit module that we call the fusion defect. For one-row shapes the inequality places both $q$-Foulkes plethysms $H_b[H_a]$ and $H_a[H_b]$ above the same polynomial $H_{ab}$, and comparing their two defects we obtain a distorted version of Bergeron's $q$-analog of Foulkes' conjecture, in which the subtracted plethysm is shifted by $q^{a(a-1)\lfloor b/2\rfloor}$.

papers.title: The $q$-Foulkes problem II: Schur positivity with high probability
papers.abstract: Bergeron's $q$-analog of Foulkes' conjecture asserts that $(H_b[H_a]-H_a[H_b])/(1-q)$ is Schur positive for $a\le b$, where $H_n$ is the (modified) Hall--Littlewood polynomial. We view this conjecture probabilistically: on each irreducible representation of $S_{ab}$, the two plethysms induce degree distributions, and positivity means that the first is stochastically smaller than the second. We prove that, for a random (Plancherel) irreducible representation and a degree sampled from its graded multiplicity, the corresponding coefficient is negative with probability at most $C\exp(-c(ab)^{1/3})$, uniformly in $a\le b$. Consequently, the $q$-Foulkes conjecture holds after deleting a fraction at most $C\exp(-c(ab)^{1/3})$ of each of the two graded modules. Additionally, we show that exact conditional means and variances yield complete positivity for explicit width and height families.

papers.title: The $q$-Foulkes problem III: On Foulkes' conjecture with a graded inner factor
papers.abstract: We show that surjectivity of the canonical map $\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^aV)\to\mathrm{Sym}^a(\mathrm{Sym}^bV)$ survives grading of the inner factor. Consequently $h_b[H_a]-H_a[h_b]$ is Schur positive whenever the canonical map is surjective, where $H_a$ is the (modified) Hall--Littlewood polynomial; the same holds for (modified) Macdonald polynomials. We prove this surjectivity for $b\ge(a-1)^2$, improving the known bound $a(a-1)$. For Bergeron's $q$-analog of Foulkes' conjecture that lets both factors be graded, we prove nonnegativity of every Schur coefficient for certain special cases. We also study the full conjecture under an expansion hypothesis on an explicit space of maps.

papers.title: The Esperanza Algorithm for Maximum Independent Set
papers.abstract: The maximum independent set problem asks for the largest set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices in an undirected graph. It is NP-hard to approximate within $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and under the Unique Games Conjecture it is hard to approximate within $O(\Delta/\log^2\Delta)$ on graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$; the Khot--Regev form of the conjecture, for which a proof has been reported but not yet peer reviewed, also rules out a $(2-\varepsilon)$-approximation of Minimum Vertex Cover. We present version 0.1.6 of \textsc{Esperanza}, which takes the better of a dynamic minimum-degree (Caro--Wei) greedy set and the complement of the \textsc{Salvador} vertex cover, and improves it by three budgeted local searches: repair-and-grow restarts at the cover vertices and at a maximum-degree vertex, chained local restarts realising $(k,k+1)$-improvements, and an iterated $(1,2)$-swap search. We prove that it runs in $O((n+m)\,\alpha_{\mathrm A}(n))$ expected time for fixed budgets, with $\alpha_{\mathrm A}$ the inverse Ackermann function. We prove that the output is a maximal independent set, that its complementary vertex cover has at most $2\tau-r$ vertices, where $\tau$ is the minimum cover size and $r$ the number of components with an edge, and that the ratio is at most $(\Delta+2)/3$ on graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$. We prove the ratio $2\sqrt n$ on every graph with $\Delta\le\sqrt n$ and on three further classes, and state it for all graphs as a conjecture, whose proof would imply $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. We also state the conjecture that the complementary cover has at most $2\tau-|M|$ vertices for the NetworkX minimum maximal matching $M$; a proof would give a $3/2$-approximation for Minimum Vertex Cover and refute the Unique Games Conjecture unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. In reproducible experiments the returned set is optimal on all $30\,000$ graphs of a suite certified by an exact integer program; on $40$ Khot--Regev YES instances with $640$ to $2\,560$ vertices the conjectured bound is certified on $38$ and open on $2$; and on $31$ bounded-degree graphs the certified ratio is at most $1.0769$ on the families with a planted independent set.

papers.title: The exponent of $p$ in $x^{p-1}-1$: Yamada's constant 283 lowered to 69
papers.abstract: Yamada (J. Number Theory 130, 2010) deduced from the method of interpolation determinants of Bugeaud and Laurent the bound $v_p(x^{p-1}-1)\le 283\,(p-1)\log y\,\log(xy)/(\log p)^2+4$, for multiplicatively independent integers $x,y$ coprime to $p$. We replace 283 by 69. The new ingredient is an elementary bound, by rearrangement, on the spread of the exponents that occur in the Liouville inequality: it at least halves the height term of Yamada's criterion, involves no congruence class, and allows the parameters to be re-optimised. The proof is complete up to the lemmas of Bugeaud–Laurent (zero lemma, analytic upper bound) and of Laurent–Mignotte–Nesterenko (bound for the polynomial), which are used as they stand. A self-contained verifier checks the numerical inequalities.

papers.title: The Fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra over nontrivially valued fields and the radius of convergence of nonarchimedean differential equations
papers.abstract: We prove a fundamental theorem for tropical partial differential equations, analogous to the fundamental theorem of tropical geometry in this context. We extend results from Aroca et al., Falkensteiner et al. and from Fink and Toghani for the case of trivial valuation as introduced by Grigoriev to differential equations with power series coefficients over any valued field. Crucial ingredients are the framework for tropical partial differential equations introduced by Giansiracusa and Mereta and a result on infinite intersections of projections of fibers of tropicalizations, which we prove using Hrushovski and Loeser's model-theoretic interpretation of Berkovich analytification. As a corollary of the fundamental theorem, we show that the radius of convergence of solutions of an ordinary differential equation over a nontrivially valued field can be computed tropically.

papers.title: The Macdonald $(q,t)$-permanent I: Algebra and positivity
papers.abstract: We introduce the Macdonald $(q,t)$-permanent, a two-parameter cycle-weighted permanent that contains the usual permanent and determinant, as well as the $\alpha$-permanent of Vere-Jones, as degenerate cases. We prove a MacMahon-type master theorem for its generating function, and determine when it induces a valid kernel on tuples of vectors. Nonnegativity of the $(q,t)$-permanent itself on semidefinite matrices turns out to be subtler: for $t=q^\alpha$ nonnegativity holds exactly at the positive Wallach exponents; for a fixed $q$ we determine the region in rank two and for higher ranks under an additional condition, while for small $q$ positivity can even reach beyond the kernel region. Whether positivity forces $t\in\{0,q,q^2,\ldots\}$ remains an intriguing open problem.

papers.title: The Macdonald $(q,t)$-permanent II: Probability laws and their regions of validity
papers.abstract: The Macdonald $(q,t)$-permanent replaces the constant cycle weight of the Vere-Jones $\alpha$-permanent by $(1-t^k)/(1-q^k)$ for a cycle of length $k$. We determine which of the probability laws built on the $\alpha$-permanent survive this deformation, and where. The scalar gamma-type law survives on the whole parameter square, but the matrix law, a compound Wishart matrix, is more fragile. We prove that it exists in every dimension exactly when $t\in\{0,q,q^2,\ldots\}$, and in dimension two exactly when $t\le q$. We conjecture that in each fixed dimension the matrix law exists exactly on the region that we show to be necessary, a $q$-analogue of Gindikin's theorem.

papers.title: The metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI announced a counterexample to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4. Here, we prove that the metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture is true in dimension 4. More precisely, let $f,g\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ be germs of reduced holomorphic functions, and let $\varphi\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ be a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism such that $\varphi(V(f))=V(g)$. We prove that if every irreducible component of the tangent cone of $V(f)$ at the origin has a singular locus of dimension at most two, then $V(f)$ and $V(g)$ have the same multiplicity at the origin. In particular, the multiplicity of complex analytic hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\leq 4$, is an embedded bi-Lipschitz invariant; the cases $n=2$ and $n=3$ were known. This extends a previous result of the author for tangent cones whose components have singular loci of dimension at most one. We also prove that two irreducible homogeneous hypersurfaces whose singular loci have dimension at most two, and which are mapped onto each other by a homeomorphism of $\mathbb{C}^n$ fixing the origin, have the same degree.

papers.title: The Möbius pseudodistance of the annulus and an improved lower bound for Korenblum's constant
papers.abstract: We show that Korenblum's constant of the Bergman space satisfies $c_2\ge 0.446$. The best published lower bound was $c_2\ge 0.4263$ (Wikström, 2026). The new ingredient is a closed form, in Jacobi theta functions, of the Möbius pseudodistance of the annulus $\{c<|z|<1\}$ between two points of the same centred circle. It separates the variables and yields three monotonicity properties, one of which, a profile inequality, combined with Kirszbraun's theorem in the hyperbolic plane, improves the constant in Wang's annular estimate. Wikström's dual moment criterion is then verified at $c=223/500$ for an explicit measure with fourteen rational atoms, in rigorous arithmetic, by a self-contained verifier. The French version of this note is dated 21 October 2026.

papers.title: The Shared Randomness Cost of Optimal One Use Loop Communication
papers.abstract: We determine the minimum support and Shannon entropy of a shared classical seed needed to attain optimal worst-message success in a specified one-use normalized-loop model. The loop contains a backward binary symmetric channel with crossover 0 < p < 1/2 and a fixed finite-dimensional forward quantum channel. Seed branches are mixed as unnormalized weights before one normalization for each message. For qubit output and interior forward trace-distance diameter, equality at the known unrestricted optimum forces every supported seed to activate exactly two message labels. The seed-cost problem becomes a fractional perfect matching problem: even message counts are optimally covered by disjoint pairs, while odd counts require a triangle and disjoint pairs. We give separate exact formulas at zero and unit diameter, prove a sufficient higher-dimensional extension of the interior result, and exhibit an erasure-channel counterexample to diameter-only seed costs in general dimension. Explicit near-optimal constructions show how the exact-attainment cost discontinuities can be avoided at finite tolerance. Compactness also gives a strict performance gap below the minimum seed support. A complete exact-certificate calculation determines the two-seed classical optimum for three messages at backward and forward crossover 1/10. These are resource-specific mathematical results, not a physical backward-communication protocol or an asymptotic capacity theorem.

papers.title: The ten minimum universal sets of MacMahon cubes
papers.abstract: A collection of six-coloured MacMahon cubes is universal if eight of its cubes can be selected to build a $2\times2\times2$ model of any target variety, with matching exterior colours and no internal matching requirement. We prove that exactly ten labelled collections attain the known minimum size of twelve, even when repeated varieties are allowed, resolving the conjectures of Johnson and Roldán. Usable-cube inequalities force a symmetric multiplicity matrix with row and column sums two; corner coverage then forces two disjoint triangles in Conway's tableau. The written proof is elementary and requires no exhaustive search. The classification and its discrete geometric interpretation are formalised in Lean 4. Exhaustive computation provides a separate check and additional target-count distributions.

papers.title: The variety of orthogonal frames
papers.abstract: An orthogonal n-frame is an ordered set of n pairwise orthogonal vectors. The set of all orthogonal n-frames in a d-dimensional quadratic vector space is an algebraic variety V(d,n). In this paper, we investigate the singularities and components of the variety V(d,n), as well as the algebraic properties of the quadratic ideal I(d,n) generated by the orthogonality relations, which cuts out V(d,n) set-theoretically. By a general result of Ananyan and Hochster, these objects satisfy increasingly strong regularity conditions when d becomes large compared to n; we establish optimal effective bounds to quantify this behavior. We give criteria for the ideal I(d,n) to be prime or a complete intersection, thereby resolving open problems proposed by Conca and Welker. We give criteria for the variety V(d,n) to be normal or factorial. We provide strong evidence in support of the conjecture that I(d,n) defines V(d,n) scheme-theoretically. As applications, we improve the existing bounds for when the Lov\'asz-Saks-Schrijver ideals of simple graphs satisfy these four properties.

papers.title: Tropicalization and Polyhedral Completions of Weyl Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct weighted and polyhedral completions of the Weyl algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field and organize them into a structure sheaf on a polyhedral $G$-site. For discretely valued fields, we prove two-sided flatness for $\Gamma$-rational polyhedral completions, yielding exact base change for finitely generated $D$-modules. For compact integral polyhedra, we also construct finite-type integral models whose special fibers are toric face rings and describe the reduction of Gauss points in terms of toric strata.

papers.title: Truncated Grassmannians: polytopes, representations, and Cauchy formulas
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to develop algebraic and combinatorial techniques for studying the geometric properties of truncated Grassmannians, a class of algebraic varieties obtained via certain projections of classical Grassmannians within their Pl\"ucker embeddings. We introduce a class of cyclic representations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of the general linear Lie algebra, which are proved to serve as duals of the homogeneous components of coordinate rings of truncated Grassmannians. We prove that the characters of these representations are computed via truncated Cauchy formulas and establish a connection with coordinate rings of complete collineations. We also construct monomial bases of these representations in terms of certain generalized chain polytopes and use the RSK correspondence to establish connections with Cauchy-type formulas and with Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.

papers.title: Turning non-smooth points into rational points
papers.abstract: In a recent paper, the author and St\"ohr established a bound on the number of iterated Frobenius pullbacks needed to transform a non-smooth purely inseparable point on a regular geometrically integral curve into a rational point. In this paper we improve this result, by establishing a new bound that is sharp in every characteristic $p>0$.

papers.title: Type classifiers
papers.abstract:
We extend dependent type theory by type classifiers and construct an interpretation in the category of contextual categories with families. Type classifiers extend contexts by type variables, complementing the usual context extensions by term variables of specified types. This allows statements with arbitrary type parameters to be formulated without assuming a universe.
  We show that substituting isomorphic types induces isomorphisms between the resulting types even in extensional type theory, giving an analogue of the invariance supplied by the univalence axiom in homotopy type theory. Omitting function types from the theory, so that all type formers are covariant, extends this naturality to arbitrary, possibly noninvertible maps.

papers.title: Uniformization of compact K\"ahler Threefolds of Zero Kodaira Dimension
papers.abstract: Given two smooth compact K\"ahler threefolds $X$ and $Y$ whose universal covers are biholomorphic, we show that $\kappa(X) = 0$ if and only if $\kappa(Y) =0$.

papers.title: Upper bounds for the Chvátal–Sankoff constants $\gamma_k$, $k\ge3$
papers.abstract: Lueker (J. ACM 56(3), 2009) constructed a family of finite-state machines $\mathcal{M}_h$ whose associated transfer matrices yield upper bounds on the Chvátal–Sankoff constants $\gamma_k$, and proved (his Theorem 3.26) that these bounds converge to $\gamma_k$ for every alphabet size $k$. He published values only for $k=2$. For $k\ge3$ the best upper bounds we were able to find in the literature in September 2026 were still those of Dančík's 1994 thesis: subsequent work generalising Lueker has generalised his Section 2, the lower bound. We implement $\mathcal{M}_h$ for arbitrary $k$. One ingredient has no binary analogue — the generating function of a truncation class when both sides of a minimal match pair are truncated — and we derive it. We then give a reduction by relative forms under which the transition multiplicities of the transfer matrix are falling factorials in $k$; one alphabet-free construction consequently determines the exact matrix for every $k$. We obtain improved upper bounds for $k=3,\dots,15$, each supported by a Collatz–Wielandt certificate verified in exact rational arithmetic, among them $\gamma_5\le0.645033$. A note added on 31 October 2026 compares these values with those of a repository made public by L. Jack on 25 October 2026.

papers.title: Weak positivity of Schur forms under decomposable curvature
papers.abstract: Griffiths's 1969 conjecture predicts positivity of Schur forms for Griffiths-positive vector bundles. Finski reduced its weak form to a sign question for the double mixed discriminant $\Phi_n(H)$ of a positive linear map. Du's rank-nine counterexample shows that $\Phi_n(H)\ge0$ fails in general. We prove $\Phi_n(H)\ge0$ for every decomposable map $H$, a sum of a completely positive and a completely copositive map, using a quaternionic Gaussian determinant representation. Combined with Finski's incidence formula, this inequality gives weak nonnegativity of every Schur form under decomposable curvature, without splitting assumptions. Beyond the decomposable cone, nonnegativity of $\Phi_k(H_{V,U})$ on every square compression is equivalent to $\Phi_n(H+S)\ge0$ for every entanglement-breaking map $S$. This class contains explicit indecomposable maps, but is nonconvex in every size $n\ge9$. We prove the nonconvexity by expressing Du's map as an average of four members, and the obstruction persists when all compression inequalities are strict.

papers.title: Weighted flip graphs from cyclic quantum mutations: pentagon inequalities and exponential separations
papers.abstract: Positive cyclic quantum mutations at a third root of unity induce an explicit weight on polygon flip graphs. We study the resulting discrepancy between minimum flip count and minimum accumulated normalization loss. Every pentagon three-to-two replacement strictly decreases weight, and in connected types $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$ every minimum-weight path is a flip geodesic. In type $A_4$, however, a six-flip path has smaller weight than the unique five-flip geodesic. A compatible positive projective gluing construction amplifies this example to an exponential success-probability separation in every connected type $A_n$, $n\ge4$. We also give a quantitative perturbation bound preserving the separation. The low-rank minimality statement has an exhaustive finite certificate; the pentagon inequality and the all-rank construction are analytic. In the associated sequential postselection model, differences of path weights determine success-probability ratios independently of the input state. The comparison holds for separately normalized exact mutation steps.

papers.title: Wigner–Yanase–Dyson Metrics Have Monotone Curvature
papers.abstract: Gibilisco and Isola conjectured that the scalar curvature of the Wigner–Yanase–Dyson metric with parameter $p$ on the invertible density matrices increases under mixing for all $p$ in some interval $(1,1+\varepsilon)$; the case $p\downarrow1$ is Petz's conjecture for the Kubo–Mori metric (resolved in a companion paper). We prove that for $p\in(1-\varepsilon,1+\varepsilon)$, with $\varepsilon>0$ independent of the dimension, the scalar curvature is a concave function of the eigenvalues and hence increases under mixing. By Dittmann's formula it suffices to prove that one symmetric function $H_p$ of three positive variables is concave, which we do by showing that $-1/H_p$ is a Stieltjes transform along every line in the positive cone, uniformly in $p$ near $1$. The value of $\varepsilon$ is not explicit.
